static int8_t ble_count_bonded_devices(void)
{
  uint8_t total = 0;
  tBleStatus ret;
  Bonded_Device_Entry_t devices[16];
  Identity_Entry_t rl_entries[16];

  // 1) Rebuild the whitelist from the bonding database (PM0271 5.3.1 step 3)
  ret = aci_gap_configure_whitelist();
  APP_DBG_MSG("\taci_gap_configure_whitelist = 0x%02X\r\n", ret);

  // 2) Fetch bonded identities (PM0271 5.3.1 step 4)
  ret = aci_gap_get_bonded_devices(&total, devices);
  if (ret != BLE_STATUS_SUCCESS)
  {
    APP_DBG_MSG("ACI_GAP_GET_BONDED_DEVICES error %x\r\n", ret);
    return -1;
  }

  if (total == 0)
  {
    APP_DBG_MSG("No previous bonded devices\r\n");
  }

  for (uint8_t k = 0; k < total; k++)
  {
    // Log for visibility
    APP_DBG_MSG("Bonded %u/%u - %s %02X:%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X:%02X\r\n",
                k + 1, total,
                devices[k].Address_Type == 0 ? "Public" : "Random",
                devices[k].Address[5], devices[k].Address[4], devices[k].Address[3],
                devices[k].Address[2], devices[k].Address[1], devices[k].Address[0]);

    rl_entries[k].Peer_Identity_Address_Type = devices[k].Address_Type;
    memcpy(rl_entries[k].Peer_Identity_Address, devices[k].Address, 6);
  }

  // 3) Add bonded identities to resolving list (PM0271 5.3.1 step 5)
  ret = aci_gap_add_devices_to_resolving_list(total, rl_entries, 1);
  if (ret != BLE_STATUS_SUCCESS)
  {
    APP_DBG_MSG("aci_gap_add_devices_to_resolving_list fail %x\r\n", ret);
    return -1;
  }

  APP_DBG_MSG("Resolving List populated with %u bonded device(s)\r\n", total);
  return (int8_t)total;
}

static void Adv_Update_Req(void)
{
  /**
   * The code shall be executed in the background as an aci command may be sent
   * The background is the only place where the application can make sure a new aci command
   * is not sent if there is a pending one
   */
  UTIL_SEQ_SetTask(1 << CFG_TASK_ADV_UPDATE_ID, CFG_SCH_PRIO_1);
}

  FS_Adv_Request(APP_BLE_FAST_ADV);

    // Find the end of the string and step back to the last non-whitespace character
    end = start + strlen(start) - 1;
    while (end > start && isspace((unsigned char)*end)) end--;

uint8_t is_all_zeros(const void *buffer, size_t size) {
    const unsigned char *byte_buffer = (const unsigned char *)buffer;

    for (size_t i = 0; i < size; i++) {
        if (byte_buffer[i] != 0) {
            return 0;
        }
    }
    return 1;
}

void FS_State_Read(void)
{
	char    buffer[100];
	size_t  len;

	char    *name;
	char    *result;
	int32_t val;

	/* Initialize persistent state */
	state.config_filename[0] = 0;
	state.temp_folder = 0;
	state.charge_current = 2;
	strcpy(state.device_name, "FlySight");
	state.enable_ble = 1;
	state.reset_ble = 1;
	memset(state.session_id, 0, 4 * 3);
	memset(state.ble_irk, 0, CONFIG_DATA_IR_LEN);
	memset(state.ble_erk, 0, CONFIG_DATA_ER_LEN);
	state.active_mode = FS_ACTIVE_MODE_DEFAULT;

	if (f_open(&stateFile, "/flysight.txt", FA_READ) != FR_OK)
		return;

	while (!f_eof(&stateFile))
	{
		f_gets(buffer, sizeof(buffer), &stateFile);

		len = strcspn(buffer, ";");
		buffer[len] = '\0';

		len = strcspn(buffer, ":");
		buffer[len] = '\0';

		name = trim(buffer);

void FS_State_Init(void)

}

void FS_State_Update(void)
{
	/* Initialize microSD */
	FS_ResourceManager_RequestResource(FS_RESOURCE_FATFS);

	/* Read persistent state */
	FS_State_Read();

	/* Write updated state */
	FS_State_Write();

	/* De-initialize microSD */
	FS_ResourceManager_ReleaseResource(FS_RESOURCE_FATFS);

	if (state.reset_ble)
	{
		/* Clear list of bonded devices */
		APP_BLE_Reset();
	}

	/* Update device name */
	APP_BLE_UpdateDeviceName();
}

const FS_State_Data_t *FS_State_Get(void)
{
	return &state;
}

void FS_State_NextSession(void)
{
	/* Increment temporary folder number */
	state.temp_folder = (state.temp_folder + 1) % 10000;

	/* Get random session ID */
	do
	{
		FS_Common_GetRandomBytes(state.session_id, 3);
	}
	while (is_all_zeros(state.session_id, 4 * 3));

	/* Write updated state */
	FS_State_Write();
}

void FS_State_SetConfigFilename(const char *filename)
{
	/* Update config filename */
	strncpy(state.config_filename, filename, sizeof(state.config_filename));

	/* Write updated state */
	FS_State_Write();
}

# FlySight 2 Firmware - Agent Guidelines

## Build Commands
- **Full build**: Use STM32CubeIDE or run `make` in Debug/Release configurations
- **Clean build**: `make clean` then `make`
- **Pre-build**: `./prebuild.sh` (generates version.h from git tags)

## Test Commands
- **Run all tests**: `cd Tests && make run`
- **Run single test**: `cd Tests && gcc -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g -o test_time test_time.c && ./test_time`
- **Test framework**: Custom macros (TEST, ASSERT_EQ) with assert.h

## Code Style Guidelines

### Naming Conventions
- **Functions**: snake_case (e.g., `normalizeGNSSTime`, `FS_Common_GetRandomBytes`)
- **Variables**: snake_case (e.g., `epoch_seconds`, `busy`)
- **Types/Enums**: PascalCase (e.g., `Mode_t`, `Operation_t`, `FS_GNSS_Data_t`)
- **Constants**: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (e.g., `ONE_HOUR`, `TIMEOUT`)
- **Files**: snake_case.c/.h (e.g., `sensor.c`, `time.h`)

### Formatting
- **Indentation**: 4 spaces (no tabs)
- **Braces**: K&R style, opening brace on same line
- **Line length**: No strict limit, break long lines logically
- **Includes**: System includes first, then local headers alphabetically

### Structure
- **Header guards**: `#ifndef NAME_H_ #define NAME_H_ ... #endif /* NAME_H_ */`
- **Copyright**: GPL v3 header in all files
- **Enums**: `typedef enum { ... } Name_t;`
- **Static variables**: Use for module-private state
- **Error handling**: Return error codes or use assertions in tests

### Best Practices
- **Types**: Use stdint.h types (uint32_t, int8_t, etc.)
- **Memory**: Careful with embedded constraints, avoid dynamic allocation
- **Threading**: Use STM32 sequencer for task management
- **Documentation**: Doxygen-style comments for public APIsCore

~~~~bash
/* TEMP-DBG: HCI event trace readable over SWD (never commit) */

'''
anchor="static BleApplicationContext_t BleApplicationContext;"

  /* TEMP-DBG */

      c |= ((uint32_t) ((evt_le_meta_event *) p_event_pckt->data)->subevent) << 16;
~~~~

**Tool: Bash** — Save debug patch, revert, apply clean privacy-mode fix

~~~~bash
SCR=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-hozakan-dev-FlySight-flysight-2-firmware--claude-worktrees-repo-status-ebc48f/5c1c2059-49eb-462a-9330-2c1db9a85699/scratchpad; cd /Users/hozakan/dev/FlySight/flysight-2-firmware/.claude/worktrees/repo-status-ebc48f && git diff STM32_WPAN/App/app_ble.c > $SCR/dbg_instr_with_e2.patch && git checkout -- STM32_WPAN/App/app_ble.c Core/Inc/app_conf.h && git status --short && python3 - <<'EOF'
p="STM32_WPAN/App/app_ble.c"
s=open(p).read()
old='''  APP_DBG_MSG("Resolving List populated with %u bonded device(s)\\r\\n", total);
  return (int8_t)total;'''
assert old in s
new='''  // 4) Let bonded peers connect with their identity address too. Entries of the
  //    resolving list default to Network Privacy mode, where the controller
  //    silently ignores a connection request that does not use a resolvable
  //    private address. Apple centrals reconnect with their public identity
  //    address, so without this a bonded macOS/iOS device never reaches us.
  for (uint8_t k = 0; k < total; k++)
  {
    ret = hci_le_set_privacy_mode(rl_entries[k].Peer_Identity_Address_Type,
                                  rl_entries[k].Peer_Identity_Address,
                                  BLE_PRIVACY_MODE_DEVICE);
    if (ret != BLE_STATUS_SUCCESS)
    {
      APP_DBG_MSG("hci_le_set_privacy_mode fail %x\\r\\n", ret);
    }
  }

  APP_DBG_MSG("Resolving List populated with %u bonded device(s)\\r\\n", total);
  return (int8_t)total;'''
s=s.replace(old,new,1)
open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF
grep -n "^#define FAST_ADV_TIMEOUT\|^#define ADV_TYPE\|^/\* Private define\|^#define " STM32_WPAN/App/app_ble.c | head -20
~~~~

    if (len == 0 || output_size < 3) {
        output[0] = '\0';
        return;
    }
    
    output[0] = '0';
    output[1] = 'x';

- (void)pollConnectionForHandle:(int)handle
                     peripheral:(CBPeripheral *)peripheral
                        attempt:(int)attempt
                    maxAttempts:(int)maxAttempts {
    dispatch_after(dispatch_time(DISPATCH_TIME_NOW, (int64_t)(0.5 * NSEC_PER_SEC)), _bleQueue, ^{
        // Check if callback was already invoked (by didConnectPeripheral delegate)
        if ([_handleCallbackInvoked[@(handle)] boolValue]) {
            NSLog(@"[CONNECT] Poll %d: callback already invoked by delegate, stopping poll", attempt);
            return;
        }

        NSLog(@"[CONNECT] Poll %d/%d: peripheral state = %ld for handle %d",
              attempt, maxAttempts, (long)peripheral.state, handle);

        if (peripheral.state == CBPeripheralStateConnected) {
            NSLog(@"[CONNECT] Poll: peripheral connected!");
            [self invokeConnectCallbackForHandle:handle status:BLE_SUCCESS];
            return;
        }

        if (attempt >= maxAttempts) {
            NSLog(@"[CONNECT] Poll: timeout after %d attempts for handle %d", maxAttempts, handle);
            // Cancel the pending CoreBluetooth connection attempt
            [_centralManager cancelPeripheralConnection:peripheral];
            [self invokeConnectCallbackForHandle:handle status:BLE_ERROR_TIMEOUT];
            return;
        }

        [self pollConnectionForHandle:handle peripheral:peripheral attempt:attempt+1 maxAttempts:maxAttempts];
    });
}

package ca.flysight.api.ble.jna

import com.sun.jna.Library
import com.sun.jna.Native
import com.sun.jna.Pointer

interface FlySightBleNative : Library {

    companion object {
        private const val LIBRARY_NAME = "flysight_ble"

        val INSTANCE: FlySightBleNative by lazy {
            try {
                Native.load(LIBRARY_NAME, FlySightBleNative::class.java) as FlySightBleNative
            } catch (e: UnsatisfiedLinkError) {
                val osName = System.getProperty("os.name")
                val osArch = System.getProperty("os.arch")
                throw RuntimeException(
                    "Failed to load native library: $LIBRARY_NAME\n" +
                    "Platform: $osName ($osArch)\n" +
                    "Make sure the library is built with './gradlew buildNativeLib' and copied to resources.\n" +
                    "JNA searches for libraries in the JAR under platform-specific paths (e.g., darwin-aarch64/).",
                    e
                )
            }
        }

        const val BLE_SUCCESS = 0

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

FlySightApi is a Kotlin Multiplatform project for communicating with FlySight devices via Bluetooth. The project targets Android, iOS, and Desktop platforms using a modular architecture.

## Module Structure

- **`:core`** - Core business logic and models shared across all platforms. Low level API
- **`:api`** - Main and high level API implementation with Bluetooth communication layer  
- **`:composeApp`** - Compose Multiplatform UI application used as sample app with platform-specific permission handling

## Key Architecture Patterns

### Platform-Specific Implementation
The project uses expect/actual declarations for platform-specific code:
- `BluetoothServiceDelegate` - Platform-specific Bluetooth implementations
- `PermissionServiceDelegate` - Platform-specific permission handling
- `ApiContext` - Platform context abstraction

### Dependency Flow
```
composeApp -> api -> core
```

### Main Interfaces
- `FlySightApi` (api module) - Main entry point for device scanning and connection. High level API
- `FlySightCore` (core module) - Core device connection logic. Low level API
- `BluetoothService` - Bluetooth abstraction
- `PermissionService` - Permission management abstraction

## Common Development Commands

### Build
```bash
./gradlew build                    # Build all modules
./gradlew :api:build               # Build specific module
./gradlew assemble                 # Assemble outputs
```

### iOS Framework Generation
```bash
./gradlew :api:linkDebugFrameworkIosArm64     # iOS ARM64 framework
./gradlew :core:linkDebugFrameworkIosArm64    # Core iOS framework
```

### Desktop Application
```bash
./gradlew :composeApp:run                     # Run desktop app
```

### Android
```bash
./gradlew :composeApp:installDebug           # Install Android app
```

## Platform-Specific Notes

- **Android**: Uses `AndroidBluetoothDevice` and permission system via Activities
- **iOS**: Generates frameworks named `apiKit` and `coreKit` 
- **Desktop**: Limited Bluetooth functionality (stub implementations)

## Key Constants

- Minimum Android SDK: 30
- Target/Compile Android SDK: 35/36
- Kotlin version: 2.1.21

abstract class BuildNativeLibTask : Exec() {
    @get:InputDirectory
    abstract val nativeInteropDir: DirectoryProperty
    
    init {
        val osName = System.getProperty("os.name").lowercase(Locale.getDefault())
        if (osName.contains("windows")) {
            commandLine("cmd", "/c", "build.bat")
        } else {
            commandLine("bash", "build.sh")
        }
    }
    
    @TaskAction
    override fun exec() {
        workingDir = nativeInteropDir.get().asFile
        
        val osName = System.getProperty("os.name").lowercase(Locale.getDefault())
        val platform = when {
            osName.contains("mac") || osName.contains("darwin") -> "macos"
            osName.contains("linux") -> "linux"
            osName.contains("windows") -> "windows"
            else -> throw GradleException("Unsupported platform: $osName")
        }
        
        val platformBuildDir = nativeInteropDir.get().asFile.resolve("build/$platform")
        platformBuildDir.mkdirs()
        
        super.exec()
    }
}

    @get:InputDirectory
    abstract val sourceDir: DirectoryProperty
    
    @get:OutputDirectory
    abstract val destDir: DirectoryProperty

        val platform = when {
            osName.contains("mac") || osName.contains("darwin") -> "macos"
            osName.contains("linux") -> "linux"
            osName.contains("windows") -> "windows"
            else -> throw GradleException("Unsupported platform: $osName")
        }

        // which it computes on the machine that RUNS. The architecture is therefore read from the
        // build JVM rather than assumed: a hard-coded "linux-x86-64" files an AArch64 library under
        // a name JNA will never look for, and the failure only surfaces much later as an
        // UnsatisfiedLinkError. JNA spells the two 64-bit architectures "aarch64" and "x86-64" on
        // all three systems. Only the spellings JNA itself normalises are accepted: it maps
        // "x86_64" and "amd64" onto "x86-64", but it does NOT map "arm64" onto "aarch64" -- it
        // would compute "linux-arm64". Accepting "arm64" here would refile the library under a
        // name JNA never looks for.

#!/bin/bash

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$( cd "$( dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" )" && pwd )"
BUILD_DIR="${SCRIPT_DIR}/build"

OS_NAME=$(uname -s)
case "${OS_NAME}" in
    Linux*)     PLATFORM=linux;;
    Darwin*)    PLATFORM=macos;;
    MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*)    PLATFORM=windows;;
    *)          echo "Unsupported platform: ${OS_NAME}"; exit 1;;
esac

echo "Building for platform: ${PLATFORM}"

mkdir -p "${BUILD_DIR}/${PLATFORM}"
cd "${BUILD_DIR}/${PLATFORM}"

cmake ../..
cmake --build . --config Release

echo "Build completed successfully for ${PLATFORM}"
echo "Library location: ${BUILD_DIR}/${PLATFORM}"

- (int)getCharacteristicCount:(int)handle serviceIndex:(int)serviceIndex {
    __block int count = 0;
    dispatch_sync(_bleQueue, ^{
        CBPeripheral *peripheral = _handleToPeripheralMap[@(handle)];
        if (!peripheral || !peripheral.services) return;
        if (serviceIndex < 0 || serviceIndex >= (int)peripheral.services.count) return;
        CBService *service = peripheral.services[serviceIndex];
        count = service.characteristics ? (int)service.characteristics.count : 0;
    });
    return count;
}

- (int)getCharacteristicUuid:(int)handle serviceIndex:(int)serviceIndex charIndex:(int)charIndex uuidOut:(char*)uuidOut uuidOutLen:(size_t)uuidOutLen {
    __block int result = BLE_ERROR_INVALID_PARAM;
    dispatch_sync(_bleQueue, ^{
        CBPeripheral *peripheral = _handleToPeripheralMap[@(handle)];
        if (!peripheral || !peripheral.services) {
            result = BLE_ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE;
            return;
        }
        if (serviceIndex < 0 || serviceIndex >= (int)peripheral.services.count) return;
        CBService *service = peripheral.services[serviceIndex];
        if (!service.characteristics || charIndex < 0 || charIndex >= (int)service.characteristics.count) return;
        CBCharacteristic *characteristic = service.characteristics[charIndex];
        const char *uuidStr = [characteristic.UUID.UUIDString UTF8String];
        strlcpy(uuidOut, uuidStr, uuidOutLen);
        result = BLE_SUCCESS;
    });
    return result;
}

- (int)getCharacteristicProperties:(int)handle serviceIndex:(int)serviceIndex charIndex:(int)charIndex {
    __block int props = 0;
    dispatch_sync(_bleQueue, ^{
        CBPeripheral *peripheral = _handleToPeripheralMap[@(handle)];
        if (!peripheral || !peripheral.services) return;
        if (serviceIndex < 0 || serviceIndex >= (int)peripheral.services.count) return;
        CBService *service = peripheral.services[serviceIndex];
        if (!service.characteristics || charIndex < 0 || charIndex >= (int)service.characteristics.count) return;
        CBCharacteristic *characteristic = service.characteristics[charIndex];
        props = (int)characteristic.properties;
    });
    return props;
}

~~~~bash
''','''    // One-shot callbacks (reads and acknowledged writes) fire after the call that registered them
    // returned. JNA frees the native closure of a callback that is no longer strongly reachable, so
    // each one is kept here until it has fired, or until the native layer refused the request.
    private val pendingCallbacks = mutableSetOf<BleCharacteristicCallback>()

    private fun retain(callback: BleCharacteristicCallback) {
        synchronized(pendingCallbacks) { pendingCallbacks.add(callback) }
    }
~~~~

# Native libraries (C/C++)

> Moved out of `CLAUDE.md` on 2026-08-27, verbatim. **Platform values** was a sibling section of
> **CocoaPods** there; it is folded in here because the `<platform>`, `<ext>` and `<jna-prefix>`
> placeholders it resolves are only ever used by the three build recipes above it. Open this file
> when you modify C/C++ sources, or when you are chasing an `UnsatisfiedLinkError` that names no
> directory.

The project uses native C/C++ libraries with automatic rebuild detection via Gradle's input hashing. Gradle tracks the hash of all source files — if any `.c`, `.cpp`, `.h`, `.m`, `.cmake`, `CMakeLists.txt`, or `build.sh` changes, the native library is automatically rebuilt. If nothing changed, the task is `UP-TO-DATE` (skipped).

## Firebase Native Library (`UserModule`)

- **Source:** `Modules/Feature/UserModule/src/nativeInterop/c/`
- **Build config:** `Modules/Feature/UserModule/src/nativeInterop/CMakeLists.txt`, `cmake/*.cmake`, `build.sh`
- **Build output:** `Modules/Feature/UserModule/src/nativeInterop/build/<platform>/libskygames_firebase.<ext>`
- **Resource output:** `Modules/Feature/UserModule/src/jvmMain/resources/<jna-prefix>/libskygames_firebase.<ext>`

Rebuild is automatic when sources change. To force a rebuild manually:
```bash
rm -f Modules/Feature/UserModule/src/nativeInterop/build/<platform>/libskygames_firebase.<ext>
./gradlew :UserModule:buildNativeFirebaseLib
```

## Text-to-speech Native Library (`AudioModule`)

- **Source:** `Modules/MiddleWare/AudioModule/src/nativeInterop/c/` (wraps eSpeak-ng)
- **Build output:** `Modules/MiddleWare/AudioModule/src/nativeInterop/build/<platform>/libskygames_tts.<ext>`
- **Resource output:** `Modules/MiddleWare/AudioModule/src/jvmMain/resources/<jna-prefix>/libskygames_tts.<ext>`

The compiled voice data goes to `src/jvmMain/resources/espeak-ng-data/`, which carries no
architecture in its name because it is data rather than machine code.

```bash
rm -f Modules/MiddleWare/AudioModule/src/nativeInterop/build/<platform>/libskygames_tts.<ext>
./gradlew :AudioModule:buildNativeTtsLib
```

## FlySight BLE Native Library (`FlySightApi/core`)

> **Checked 2026-08-27:** `Libs/FlySightApi` is a git submodule and it is **not initialised** in
> this checkout — `ls -a Libs/FlySightApi` shows only `.` and `..`, and `git submodule status`
> prints `-40f162ff…`, the leading `-` meaning uninitialised. Every path in this subsection, and
> the `FlySightApi/core` half of **Platform values** below, is absent from the working tree until
> `git submodule update --init --recursive` has run. `settings.gradle.kts` declares
> `includeBuild("Libs/FlySightApi")` regardless, so it cannot resolve in that state.

- **Source:** `Libs/FlySightApi/core/src/nativeInterop/c/`
- **Build output:** `Libs/FlySightApi/core/src/nativeInterop/build/<platform>/libflysight_ble.<ext>`
- **Resource output:** `Libs/FlySightApi/core/src/desktopMain/resources/<jna-prefix>/libflysight_ble.<ext>`

To force a rebuild after modifying native source code:
```bash
rm -f Libs/FlySightApi/core/src/nativeInterop/build/<platform>/libflysight_ble.<ext>
./gradlew -p Libs/FlySightApi :core:buildNativeLib
```

| Linux x86-64  | linux       | so       | linux-x86-64      |

and uses to look the library up in the classpath. It is derived from the build JVM's `os.arch` —

package ca.flysight.internal.bluetooth

import ca.flysight.api.ble.KmpBleSocket
import ca.flysight.api.ble.task.WriteNoResponseSystemCallbackPolicy
import ca.flysight.api.ble.jna.BleDevice
import ca.flysight.api.ble.jna.BleScanCallback
import ca.flysight.api.ble.jna.FlySightBleNative
import ca.flysight.api.core.model.FlySightInfo
import ca.flysight.api.core.tools.log.FlySightLogger
import com.sun.jna.Pointer
import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.channels.awaitClose
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.callbackFlow
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap

class DesktopBluetoothServiceDelegate(
    private val apiScope: CoroutineScope,
    private val logger: FlySightLogger
) : BluetoothServiceDelegate {

    private var isInitialized = false

    init {
        val result = FlySightBleNative.INSTANCE.ble_init()
        if (result != FlySightBleNative.BLE_SUCCESS) {
            val errorMsg = FlySightBleNative.INSTANCE.ble_get_error_string(result)
            throw RuntimeException("Failed to initialize BLE: $errorMsg (code: $result)")
        }
        isInitialized = true
    }

    override val platformPolicyPick: WriteNoResponseSystemCallbackPolicy =
        WriteNoResponseSystemCallbackPolicy.IgnoreSystemCallback

    override fun scan(): Flow<List<BluetoothDeviceInfo>> = callbackFlow {
        logger.d { "[SCAN] scan() called" }

        if (!isInitialized) {
            logger.e { "[SCAN] ERROR: BLE library not initialized" }
            throw IllegalStateException("BLE library not initialized")
        }

        val discoveredDevices = ConcurrentHashMap<String, BluetoothDeviceInfo>()

        val scanCallback = object : BleScanCallback {
            override fun invoke(device: BleDevice, userData: Pointer?) {
                try {
                    val name = device.getNameString()
                    val address = device.getAddressString()
                    val rssi = device.rssi
                    val manufacturerIdStr = device.getManufacturerIdString()

                    if (manufacturerIdStr == "0xDB09" || manufacturerIdStr == "0x09DB") {
                        logger.i { "[SCAN] ✅ FlySight device found: '$name' ($address) RSSI: $rssi dBm" }
                        val deviceInfo = BluetoothDeviceInfo(
                            name = name,
                            address = address,
                            rssi = rssi
                        )
                        if (discoveredDevices.put(deviceInfo.address, deviceInfo) != deviceInfo) {
                            trySend(discoveredDevices.values.toList())
                        }
                    } else {
                        logger.d { "[SCAN] ❌ Filtered out (not FlySight): '$name' mfgId='$manufacturerIdStr'" }
[... 42 lines omitted ...]
        return ca.flysight.api.ble.DesktopKmpBleSocket(
            bleDevice, 
            scope.coroutineContext[kotlinx.coroutines.Job] ?: kotlinx.coroutines.Job()
        )
    }

    fun cleanup() {
        if (isInitialized) {
            FlySightBleNative.INSTANCE.ble_cleanup()
            isInitialized = false
        }
    }
}

# Ticket: harmoniser le `connect()` entre Android, Desktop et iOS

## Contexte

On a déjà harmonisé le `disconnect()` des trois `KmpBleSocket` dans `AbstractKmpBleSocket` (commonMain, `Libs/FlySightApi/ble/src/commonMain/kotlin/ca/flysight/api/ble/AbstractKmpBleSocket.kt`). Le `connect()` est resté platform-specific avec plusieurs divergences à réduire.

## Constat

**Android** ([AndroidKmpBleSocket.kt](../../Libs/FlySightApi/ble/src/androidMain/kotlin/ca/flysight/api/ble/AndroidKmpBleSocket.kt))
- `bluetoothGatt`/`kmpGatt` sont assignés *synchroneously* dans `connect()` parce que `BluetoothDevice.connectGatt()` retourne le handle immédiatement (contrainte d'API Android).
- Pas de timeout. Si le callback `onConnectionStateChange(Connected)` ne fire jamais, `connect()` pend indéfiniment.
- Pas de fallback sur erreur : rien ne nettoie `bluetoothGatt` si la connexion finit par échouer avant que le callback ne remplace Connected par autre chose.

**Desktop** ([DesktopKmpBleSocket.kt](../../Libs/FlySightApi/ble/src/desktopMain/kotlin/ca/flysight/api/ble/DesktopKmpBleSocket.kt))
- Assigne `connectionHandle` / `_gatt` *dans le callback* natif `BleConnectCallback` (handle arrive en paramètre).
- Timeout via `withTimeoutOrNull(35_000L)`. Sur timeout, appelle `ble_disconnect` avec un callback noop, puis `handleNativeDisconnectEvent()` pour forcer la cleanup.

**iOS** ([AppleKmpBleSocket.kt](../../Libs/FlySightApi/ble/src/appleMain/kotlin/ca/flysight/api/ble/AppleKmpBleSocket.kt))
- Vérifie l'état du `CBPeripheral` avant d'appeler `centralManager.connectPeripheral`. Trois branches : déjà connecté, déjà en cours de connexion, disconnecté.
- Pas de timeout.
- Beaucoup de `NSLog` de debug (≈ une dizaine d'appels par `connect()`) qui pourraient passer par `FlySightLogger` pour être retained dans `RetainingLogger` et accessibles via le broadcast ADB.

## Mission d'investigation

1. **Helper commun `handleNativeConnectEvent()`** — étudier la possibilité d'extraire dans `AbstractKmpBleSocket` la logique commune « un native connect callback est arrivé avec un status → resume la continuation + émettre `ConnectionStateChange(Connected/Disconnected)` ». Android appelle déjà ce chemin depuis `onConnectionStateChange(Connected)`, Desktop depuis son `BleConnectCallback`, iOS depuis `onConnected()`. Vérifier que la signature commune est viable malgré les divergences (Android n'a pas de "status" standardisé, iOS est toujours Success).

2. **Timeout uniforme sur `connect()`** — ajouter un `withTimeoutOrNull(CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS)` dans le chemin commun (Android et iOS n'en ont pas aujourd'hui). Valeur suggérée : 35s comme Desktop. Sur timeout, forcer un cleanup (via `handleNativeDisconnectEvent()` ?) pour que le prochain `connect()` puisse re-allouer.

3. **Rationaliser les logs iOS** — remplacer les `NSLog` de debug par des appels à `FlySightLogger`. Garder les messages informatifs, supprimer les dumps verbeux du peripheral state à chaque invocation. À ce stade `AppleKmpBleSocket` ne reçoit pas de `FlySightLogger` dans son ctor : il faudra l'y ajouter (et plomber depuis `AppleBluetoothServiceDelegate.createBluetoothSocketDelegate`).

4. **Android : `bluetoothGatt` vs `kmpGatt` assignés avant le succès** — réfléchir à s'il y a un intérêt à séparer "gatt alloué mais pas encore connecté" de "gatt alloué et connecté". Aujourd'hui `isGattAllocated()` retourne `true` dès que `connectGatt()` a retourné, même si la connexion est encore en cours. Si `connect()` échoue (callback jamais reçu ou status=Failure), il faut s'assurer que `cleanupNativeResources()` est bien appelé pour libérer `bluetoothGatt`.

## Non-goals

- Ne pas changer les APIs natives elles-mêmes (BluetoothGatt vs FlySightBleNative vs CBCentralManager resteront divergents).
- Ne pas modifier les timings du cycle de vie du scan / du ping / de la découverte des services.
- Ne pas réécrire la chaîne complète `connect → mtu → discover → subscribe` dans `BleDeviceSocket`.

~~~~bash
    """GPIOC for PC12: a button that pulls the pin low when pressed, otherwise the pull-up wins."""

    GPIOC = vbus.GPIOC

    def __init__(self, moder=0xFFFFFFFF, odr=0x1000):
        self.moder = moder          # reset value of GPIOC.MODER: every pin an input
        self.odr = odr
        self.writes = []

    def idr(self):
        bit = 1 << vbus.BUTTON_PIN
        out = (self.moder >> (2 * vbus.BUTTON_PIN)) & 0b11 == 0b01
        high = (self.odr & bit) != 0 if out else True
        return bit if high else 0

    def _word(self, addr):
        return {self.GPIOC: self.moder, self.GPIOC + 0x10: self.idr(), self.GPIOC + 0x14: self.odr}[addr]

    def read(self, *specs):
        values = []
        for addr, width in specs:
            if width == 8:
                base = addr & ~3
                values.append((self.moder >> (8 * (addr - base))) & 0xFF)
            else:
                values.append(self._word(addr))
        return values

    def write8(self, addr, value):
        shift = 8 * (addr - self.GPIOC)
        self.writes.append(("w8", addr, value))
        self.moder = (self.moder & ~(0xFF << shift)) | (value << shift)

    def write32(self, addr, value, check=True):
        assert addr == self.GPIOC + 0x18
        self.writes.append(("w32", addr, value))
        self.odr = (self.odr | (value & 0xFFFF)) & ~(value >> 16)
~~~~

1:# FlySight 2 test CLI (ST-Link)
2:
3:`vbus.py` drives a FlySight 2 through its ST-Link, so firmware can be tested
4:without touching the USB cable. There is no CLI over USB: the device only
5:enumerates as mass storage.
6:
7:It makes the firmware believe the USB cable was unplugged or plugged back in,
8:while the cable stays connected. It takes over `VBUS_DIV` (PA2), the pin the
9:firmware uses to detect USB power (`FlySight/vbus.c`), so the real code path
10:runs: EXTI2 → mode state machine → `FS_USBMode_Init` / `FS_USBMode_DeInit`.
11:
12:```bash
13:python vbus.py status                     # what the firmware and the host see
14:python vbus.py unplug                     # firmware sees VBUS low, host loses the device
15:python vbus.py plug                       # real VBUS again, host re-enumerates
16:python vbus.py cycle -n 20 --off 1 --on 1 # soak test, checks every transition
17:python vbus.py reset                      # reset the MCU (clears any override)
18:python vbus.py reset-probe                # recover a stuck ST-Link
19:```
20:
21:`unplug` and `plug` wait for the firmware (USB clock and D+ pull-up, read over SWD)
22:and for the host (`ioreg` on macOS, sysfs on Linux) to react, and print how long it
23:took. `cycle` also fails if the firmware faulted (CFSR/HFSR) and always gives the pin
24:back on exit, including on Ctrl-C. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 a check failed, 2 error.
25:
26:## Requirements
27:
28:- Python 3.7+, no packages to install.
29:- STM32CubeProgrammer or STM32CubeIDE (`STM32_Programmer_CLI` is found automatically,
30:  or pass `--programmer` / set `STM32_PROGRAMMER_CLI`) and an ST-Link on the SWD pins.
31:- **A firmware built with `CFG_DEBUGGER_SUPPORTED=1`** (CubeMX: STM32_WPAN → Debugger,
32:  or `Core/Inc/app_conf.h`). Otherwise `APPD_Init` switches PA13/PA14 to analog and
33:  disables debug in low-power modes, and the probe cannot reach the MCU while it runs
34:  (the tool reports this after `--swd-timeout`, default 10 s).
35:
36:## Notes
37:
38:- The override lives in the GPIO registers: it survives the script exiting and is
39:  cleared by any reset. Booting with VBUS low cannot be simulated this way, because
40:  the firmware reconfigures PA2 during start-up.
41:- Use `--vid` / `--pid` if the USB descriptor changes, `--no-host` when the cable is
42:  not plugged into the machine running the script, `--sn` with several ST-Links.
43:- The ST-Link can get stuck when an SWD access is interrupted (libusb timeouts,
44:  `ST-LINK SN : -`). `reset-probe` resets it at USB level; unplugging it also works.
45:
46:## Tests
47:
48:The tool's own tests need no hardware:
49:
50:```bash
51:python -m unittest test_vbus
52:```

```bash

python vbus.py cycle -n 20 --off 1 --on 1 # soak test, checks every transition

```

`unplug` and `plug` wait for the firmware (USB clock and D+ pull-up, read over SWD)
and for the host (`ioreg` on macOS, sysfs on Linux) to react, and print how long it
took. `button` drives the user button (PC12, pressed when low) the same way. Only the
sleep mode reacts to it, so `unplug` first; the default two clicks start BLE pairing mode
(30 s, the FlySight advertises the pairing flag). `cycle` also fails if the firmware faulted (CFSR/HFSR) and always gives the pin
back on exit, including on Ctrl-C. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 a check failed, 2 error.

7:The interface utilizes standard BLE GATT services where applicable, but primarily relies on custom services for its core functionality. Familiarity with BLE concepts (GATT, Services, Characteristics, UUIDs, Notifications, Writes, Bonding, Security Modes) is recommended.
13:*   **Firmware:** A FlySight 2 unit running firmware version `v2024.11.11.release_candidate` or later is recommended to ensure compatibility with the features described here, especially the pairing mechanism and connection timeout. Firmware updates can be performed via the [online tool](https://flysight.ca/firmware/?include_beta=true). Note that different hardware batches (B1-B5, identifiable via `flysight.txt` or serial number) require specific firmware builds.
14:*   **BLE Client:** A BLE central device (e.g., smartphone, computer) with a compatible BLE stack and application, supporting secure connections (pairing/bonding) and configurable MTU.
18:### Pairing, Bonding, and Security
20:FlySight 2 employs BLE security features (bonding and whitelisting) to prevent unauthorized access.
22:1.  **Pairing Request Mode:**
23:    *   To initiate pairing with a *new* central device, the FlySight 2 must be put into "Pairing Request Mode".
26:    *   **Advertising:** In this mode, the FlySight advertises as "limited discoverable" and includes specific manufacturer data indicating pairing mode is active (`0xDB0901`, see Advertising section).
27:    *   **Duration:** Pairing request mode lasts for 30 seconds, or until a BLE connection is established, or until the button is pressed again (which cancels it and returns to Idle).
28:    *   **Functionality:** While in this mode, *any* central device can connect and initiate pairing/bonding. The whitelist filter is temporarily disabled.
30:2.  **Whitelisting (Filter Accept List):**
31:    *   FlySight 2 uses the BLE "filter accept list" (based on the bonded device list). Outside of Pairing Request Mode, it only accepts connections from devices on this list (i.e., devices it has previously bonded with).
32:    *   **Adding Devices:** When a central device successfully completes the bonding process initiated during Pairing Request Mode, its address/identity is added to the FlySight's internal bonded device list, effectively whitelisting it for future connections.
33:    *   **Storage:** The bonded device list (including security keys like IRK/ERK) is stored persistently in the FlySight 2's non-volatile memory.
35:3.  **Bonding Process:**
36:    *   **Initiation:** After connecting to a FlySight 2 in Pairing Request Mode, the central device *must* initiate bonding to establish a secure, encrypted link and be added to the whitelist.
37:    *   **Security:** FlySight 2 requests **Security Mode 1, Level 2** (Authenticated pairing with encryption, No MITM protection). It uses the **Just Works** association model (as it has NoInput/NoOutput capabilities).
38:    *   **Triggering Pairing:** Since the peripheral (FlySight) cannot force pairing, the central device must trigger it. A reliable method is to attempt to **read a secure characteristic** (e.g., `FT_Packet_In` UUID `00000002-8e22-4541-9d4c-21edae82ed19`) immediately after connecting. FlySight 2 requires encryption for accessing user data characteristics. This read attempt will fail with an "insufficient authentication/encryption" error from the FlySight's BLE stack, which typically prompts the central device's OS/BLE stack to initiate the pairing/bonding procedure (often showing a system dialog to the user like "Pair with FlySight?").
39:    *   **Completion:** Once pairing is complete, the central device should store the bonding information (keys) provided by the BLE stack for future use. The FlySight stores the central's identity.
42:    *   Once a central device is bonded and whitelisted, it can reconnect to the FlySight 2 even when the FlySight is *not* in Pairing Request Mode (e.g., when the LED is off or solid green), provided the FlySight is advertising (typically in

---
name: skygames-ble-link-investigation
description: Root cause and test setup for the macOS ⇄ FlySight 2 BLE reconnection failures (bonded FlySight never reachable from macOS), plus the SkyGames app-side fixes
metadata:
  type: project
---

**Root cause (found 2026-10-07):** macOS reconnects to a bonded FlySight from its *public identity address*. `ble_count_bonded_devices()` in `STM32_WPAN/App/app_ble.c` puts bonded peers in the controller's resolving list, whose entries default to **Network Privacy mode**: a connection request from an identity address (not an RPA) is silently ignored. The FlySight sees nothing (no HCI event), macOS times out after 30 s (`BLE_ERROR_TIMEOUT`, -10). The same applies in pairing mode and in idle mode. Fix: `hci_le_set_privacy_mode(type, addr, 1)` (device privacy) for each bonded entry right after `aci_gap_add_devices_to_resolving_list`. A/B on hardware: 0 successes before, 12/12 and 8/8 reconnects after. The bug is on master too, not a branch regression.

**Why:** the user's complaint was "problèmes de liaison entre l'app SkyGames sur macOS et le flysight"; this was the main one.

**How to apply / test setup:**
- Probe harness lives outside the repos in the session scratchpad (`blelab/BleProbe.app`, built from the SkyGames native sources with `build_probe.sh`); it needs a one-time macOS Bluetooth permission click (TCC) after every rebuild, and an unlocked screen.
- Pairing dialog "Connection Request from: FlySight" belongs to `BluetoothUIServer`. It cannot be answered while the Mac is locked (`CGSSessionScreenIsLocked`), and AX queries on it hang then. Never type a password to unlock.
- `vbus.py button click -n 2` (PC12) = pairing mode; FlySight bonds are cleared with `Reset_BLE: 1` in flysight.txt plus an unplug/plug.
- To see FlySight-side HCI events without a sniffer: temporary volatile ring buffer in `SVCCTL_App_Notification`, read with `STM32_Programmer_CLI mode=HOTPLUG -r8` (needs CFG_DEBUGGER_SUPPORTED=1). Skip ecode 0x0004 (radio activity) or it floods the ring.
- The identity address is regenerated at every boot (`CFG_STATIC_RANDOM_ADDRESS` undefined); resolution still works through the IRK, so this was not the cause, but it is worth knowing.
- `FS_State_Read` returns early when flysight.txt cannot be opened, leaving IRK/ERK all zero for that boot (then regenerated at the next boot, orphaning bonds). Not fixed yet; same on master.

## Assistant (06:04)

J'ai trouvé la cause principale des échecs de liaison macOS ⇄ FlySight et je l'ai corrigée dans le firmware. Les corrections côté application SkyGames sont écrites et elles compilent, mais je n'ai pas pu les tester sur le Mac. Ton Mac est verrouillé depuis environ une heure, donc je n'ai pas pu valider l'invite d'autorisation Bluetooth ni les fenêtres d'appairage. Aucun commit n'a été fait.

**Cause racine**
- macOS se reconnecte à un FlySight déjà lié avec son adresse publique d'identité. Le FlySight l'a vu sur le lien radio : `peer=FC:B2:14:DB:73:11`, c'est l'adresse de ton Mac.
- Dans le firmware, les appareils liés sont placés dans la liste de résolution du contrôleur, en mode « vie privée réseau » par défaut. Dans ce mode, le contrôleur ignore sans rien signaler toute demande de connexion qui ne vient pas d'une adresse privée résolvable.
- Résultat : le FlySight ne voit rien (aucun événement) et macOS abandonne après 30 s avec le code −10. C'était vrai en mode pairing comme au repos.
- Ce défaut existe aussi sur `master`, ce n'est pas une régression de cette branche.

**Correctif firmware**
- [app_ble.c](STM32_WPAN/App/app_ble.c:1644) : après l'ajout à la liste de résolution, `hci_le_set_privacy_mode(..., device)` pour chaque appareil lié.
- Mesure sur la carte, même état de liaison : 0 reconnexion réussie avant le correctif, 12 sur 12 puis 8 sur 8 après.
- [state.c](FlySight/state.c:142) : sans `flysight.txt`, le firmware démarrait avec des clés BLE (IRK/ERK) entièrement à zéro, puis en changeait au démarrage suivant, ce qui orphelinait les liaisons. Mesuré avant (zéros dans le fichier) et après (clés aléatoires, identiques après un second reset).
- J'ai aussi complété [vbus.py](Scripts/cli/vbus.py) (commande `button`), ses tests (25 passent), le [README](Scripts/cli/README.md) et [Docs/ble.md](Docs/ble.md).

**Correctifs côté SkyGames**
Ils sont dans le sous-module `Libs/FlySightApi`, non commités, avec le code Objective-C (`ble_macos.m`) et Kotlin. Le build de la bibliothèque native macOS et la compilation Kotlin passent.
- Une déconnexion non demandée (FlySight éteint ou hors de portée) n'était jamais signalée à l'application. Elle l'est maintenant, via une nouvelle fonction `ble_set_disconnect_callback`, ajoutée aussi sous Linux et Windows. Je n'ai pu compiler ni l'une ni l'autre de ces deux versions.
- Après un délai de connexion dépassé, la connexion en attente était annulée côté système sans être libérée côté application ; elle est maintenant libérée.
- Les lectures, écritures et découvertes de services en cours échouent tout de suite à la perte du lien, au lieu de rester bloquées jusqu'à leur délai.
- L'erreur CoreBluetooth 14 (« le FlySight a oublié la liaison ») est maintenant reconnue sur macOS et remonte jusqu'à l'application, comme sur iOS.
- Les callbacks JNA de lecture et d'écriture pouvaient être libérés par le ramasse-miettes avant d'être appelés, ce qui peut faire planter la JVM. Ils sont maintenant conservés jusqu'à leur appel.

**Ce qui reste à faire, avec toi devant le Mac**
- Déverrouille le Mac et clique une fois sur « Autoriser » pour `BleProbe` (la sonde de test, signée avec ton certificat de développement, donc les recompilations suivantes ne redemanderont rien). Lance ensuite `blelab/validate_app_layer.sh`, dans le dossier de travail temporaire de la session, qui vérifie la déconnexion non sollicitée et le nettoyage après délai dépassé.
- Je n'ai pas pu refaire un cycle complet suppression → appairage → reconnexion avec le firmware corrigé. L'appairage demande de cliquer sur la fenêtre « Connection Request », et l'écran verrouillé la bloque. Le test de reconnexion après liaison, lui, est fait.
- Pour que le FlySight « HozakaN » en profite, il faut flasher le nouveau firmware dessus.

La carte est branchée et exécute le firmware corrigé. Il a été compilé avec le support du débogueur, une réserve de test dans le dossier de travail temporaire. Son `flysight.txt` d'origine est restauré. Veux-tu que je commite, et si oui, tout dans un seul commit ou séparément par sujet ? Je les ferai sans mention d'IA, comme convenu.

1	# FlySight 2 BLE Interface Developer Documentation
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	This document describes the Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) interface for the FlySight 2 device. This interface allows applications to interact with the FlySight 2 for file access (reading, writing, deleting files and directories), accessing real-time sensor data, and managing device state.
6	
7	The interface utilizes standard BLE GATT services where applicable, but primarily relies on custom services for its core functionality. Familiarity with BLE concepts (GATT, Services, Characteristics, UUIDs, Notifications, Writes, Bonding, Security Modes) is recommended.
8	
9	**Note:** This interface is under active development. Details may change in future firmware versions. This documentation reflects the state based on developer discussions and firmware code (`v2024.11.11.release_candidate` or similar, check `flysight.txt` for exact version).
10	
11	## Prerequisites
12	
13	*   **Firmware:** A FlySight 2 unit running firmware version `v2024.11.11.release_candidate` or later is recommended to ensure compatibility with the features described here, especially the pairing mechanism and connection timeout. Firmware updates can be performed via the [online tool](https://flysight.ca/firmware/?include_beta=true). Note that different hardware batches (B1-B5, identifiable via `flysight.txt` or serial number) require specific firmware builds.
14	*   **BLE Client:** A BLE central device (e.g., smartphone, computer) with a compatible BLE stack and application, supporting secure connections (pairing/bonding) and configurable MTU.
15	
16	## Core Concepts
17	
18	### Pairing, Bonding, and Security
19	
20	FlySight 2 employs BLE security features (bonding and whitelisting) to prevent unauthorized access.
21	
22	1.  **Pairing Request Mode:**
23	    *   To initiate pairing with a *new* central device, the FlySight 2 must be put into "Pairing Request Mode".
24	    *   **Activation:** While the unit is off (Idle Mode, LED is off), perform **two short presses** of the power button.
25	    *   **Indication:** The **green LED** will pulse slowly (2-second period).
26	    *   **Advertising:** In this mode, the FlySight advertises as "limited discoverable" and includes specific manufacturer data indicating pairing mode is active (`0xDB0901`, see Advertising section).
27	    *   **Duration:** Pairing request mode lasts for 30 seconds, or until a BLE connection is established, or until the button is pressed again (which cancels it and returns to Idle).
28	    *   **Functionality:** While in this mode, *any* central device can connect and initiate pairing/bonding. The whitelist filter is temporarily disabled.
29	
30	2.  **Whitelisting (Filter Accept List):**
31	    *   FlySight 2 uses the BLE "filter accept list" (based on the bonded device list). Outside of Pairing Request Mode, it only accepts connections from devices on this list (i.e., devices it has previously bonded with).
32	    *   **Adding Devices:** When a central device successfully completes the bonding process initiated during Pairing Request Mode, its address/identity is added to the FlySight's internal bonded device list, effectively whitelisting it for future connections.
33	    *   **Storage:** The bonded device list (including security keys like IRK/ERK) is stored persistently in the FlySight 2's non-volatile memory.
34	    *   **Reconnecting with an identity address:** Bonded devices are also loaded into the controller's resolving list in *device privacy* mode, so a central may reconnect either from a resolvable private address or from its identity address. macOS connects from its public identity address; in the default *network privacy* mode the controller silently ignores such a request and the central just times out.
35

37	    *   **Initiation:** After connecting to a FlySight 2 in Pairing Request Mode, the central device *must* initiate bonding to establish a secure, encrypted link and be added

~~~~bash

p="ble_macos.m"
s=open(p).read()
old='''        // The peer no longer holds the pairing while this Mac still does, so encryption can never
        // succeed until the user removes the device in System Settings and pairs it again.
        if (error.code == CBErrorPeerRemovedPairingInformation) {
            return BLE_ERROR_PAIRING_REMOVED;
        }'''
new='''        // The peer no longer holds the pairing while this Mac still does, so encryption can never
        // succeed until the user removes the device in System Settings and pairs it again. macOS
        // reports it as 14 when the peer answers "key missing", and as 15 ("Failed to encrypt the
        // connection") when the peer just drops the link, which is what a FlySight does.
        if (error.code == CBErrorPeerRemovedPairingInformation ||
            error.code == CBErrorEncryptionTimedOut) {
            return BLE_ERROR_PAIRING_REMOVED;
        }'''
assert old in s
open(p,"w").write(s.replace(old,new))
EOF
~~~~

## Ce que j'ai corrigé

**1. Firmware : le Mac ne pouvait plus se reconnecter à un FlySight déjà appairé (la cause principale)**
- Le FlySight garde une liste des appareils appairés. Pour ceux-ci, sa puce radio exige par défaut qu'ils se présentent avec une adresse « déguisée », qui change régulièrement.
- Le Mac se reconnecte avec sa vraie adresse fixe. La puce du FlySight ignore alors la demande sans rien signaler : le FlySight ne voit rien, et le Mac abandonne au bout de 30 s.
- J'ai ajouté un appel dans [app_ble.c](STM32_WPAN/App/app_ble.c:1644) qui autorise les deux types d'adresse pour les appareils appairés.
- Résultat mesuré : avant, aucune reconnexion ne réussissait. Après, 30 sur 30.

**2. Firmware : carte SD sans `flysight.txt`** ([state.c](FlySight/state.c:142))
- Au premier démarrage, les clés Bluetooth étaient à zéro. Au démarrage suivant, elles devenaient aléatoires. Un appairage fait au premier démarrage était donc perdu.
- Maintenant les clés sont créées dès le premier démarrage.

**3. Application SkyGames sur Mac**
- Elle n'était pas prévenue quand le FlySight se déconnectait de lui-même (éteint, hors de portée). C'est corrigé.
- Après un délai dépassé, la tentative de connexion restait en mémoire. C'est nettoyé.
- Les lectures et écritures en cours restaient bloquées quand le lien tombait. Elles échouent maintenant tout de suite.
- Une liaison obsolète est maintenant reconnue et signalée comme « liaison supprimée ». L'application peut donc proposer d'oublier l'appareil.

**4. Outils de test**
- Commande `button` dans [vbus.py](Scripts/cli/vbus.py), avec tests et documentation.

## Ce que je te demandais

Le document dit que `Reset_BLE` efface la liste des appareils appairés **et** la clé d'identité du FlySight. C'est cette clé qui permet au Mac de reconnaître le FlySight malgré ses changements d'adresse. Le code, lui, n'efface que la liste.

La conséquence : après un `Reset_BLE`, si tu n'oublies pas le FlySight sur le Mac, le Mac le reconnaît encore. Il essaie alors de réutiliser son ancienne liaison, que le FlySight a oubliée, et la connexion échoue. C'est ce que j'ai observé pendant mes tests.

Changer la clé au reset réglerait ça. Mais la nouvelle clé ne serait utilisée qu'au redémarrage suivant du FlySight. Si tu appaires entre le reset et ce redémarrage, la liaison serait faite avec l'ancienne clé et casserait au redémarrage. D'où mon hésitation.

Deux options :
- **A.** On corrige le document : « `Reset_BLE` efface les appareils appairés, il faut aussi oublier le FlySight sur le Mac ». Je recommande celle-ci : c'est sans risque.
- **B.** On change la clé au reset et on force un redémarrage du FlySight juste après. C'est plus invasif.

## Ce qui n'est pas corrigé

Ton scénario (appairage, déconnexion, mode pairing à nouveau, identifiant Mac qui change) se reproduit chez moi. Je n'ai pas encore de correctif sûr. Il reste à savoir si l'application doit mieux gérer ce changement d'identifiant, ou si le firmware peut l'éviter.

Quelle option pour le document ? Et veux-tu que je creuse ton scénario en priorité ?

## Assistant (10:08)

Ta correction est justifiée, et mon rapport précédent était mauvais. Voici ce que j'ai vérifié.

## La correction firmware est nécessaire

J'ai testé ton flux exact (appairage sur le Mac, déconnexion, FlySight en mode pairing à nouveau, connexion depuis le Mac). Même carte, liaisons effacées des deux côtés avant chaque série :

| Firmware | Appairage | Reconnexion immédiate | Connexion en mode pairing (3 essais) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `master`, sans aucune modification | OK | échec (−10) | 0 sur 3 |
| Branche, sans ma correction | OK | échec (−10) | 0 sur 3 |
| Branche, avec ma correction | OK | OK (série propre précédente) | 3 sur 3 |

Ton problème se reproduit donc sur `master`, et ma correction le règle. Le FlySight, lui, voit le Mac se connecter avec son adresse publique (`peer=FC:B2:14:DB:73:11`, pas d'adresse déguisée).

## Les deux types d'adresse

- **Adresse privée résolvable** : une adresse « déguisée » qui change régulièrement, que le FlySight peut rattacher à un appareil appairé. Android se connecte avec celle-ci, d'où un flux qui marche chez toi.
- **Adresse d'identité** : l'adresse fixe de l'appareil. macOS se connecte avec celle-ci.

Par défaut, le contrôleur radio du FlySight n'accepte, pour un appareil appairé, que la première. Il ignore l'autre sans le signaler. Ma correction ([app_ble.c](STM32_WPAN/App/app_ble.c:1644)) active le mode « device privacy » pour chaque appareil appairé : le contrôleur accepte alors les deux.

## Corrections de mes erreurs

- Je n'ai pas d'autre FlySight : mon hypothèse du « voisin » était fausse. Je ne sais pas encore expliquer les identifiants fantômes que le Mac attribue parfois à ma carte.
- Tu as raison sur `Reset_BLE` : le comportement actuel est normal, je n'y touche pas.

## Ce que j'ai modifié

- Firmware : cette correction, et `state.c` (clés Bluetooth créées dès le premier démarrage quand `flysight.txt` manque).
- Application SkyGames macOS : elle est prévenue des déconnexions du FlySight, nettoie les connexions échouées et signale une liaison obsolète, sans bloquer.
- Test des modifications SkyGames : déconnexion non sollicitée et nettoyage après délai dépassé validés sur la carte. La bibliothèque native et le Kotlin compilent.
- Outils : commande `button` dans `vbus.py`, avec tests et documentation.

La carte est branchée avec le firmware corrigé. Le Mac et la carte sont appairés de façon cohérente, tu peux tester directement dans l'application. Je n'ai rien commité.

Veux-tu que je commite, et si oui en un seul commit ou séparément (firmware, CLI, SkyGames) ?

The board currently runs the fixed firmware, built with <code>CFG_DEBUGGER_SUPPORTED=1</code> (needed by the SWD tooling, not committed) and its original <code>flysight.txt</code>.</p>

<h2 id="reproduce">11. How to check it yourself</h2>

<ol>
  <li>Flash the branch (with the fix). Pair the Mac with the FlySight as usual (double-press, accept the macOS dialog).</li>
  <li>Close the connection, then double-press again to re-enter pairing mode, and connect from the SkyGames macOS app. It connects.</li>
  <li>For the comparison, flash <code>origin/master</code> and repeat from a clean state (<code>Reset_BLE: 1</code> on the FlySight, and "Forget This Device" for the FlySight in macOS System Settings &rarr; Bluetooth): pairing works, then the connection times out after 30 seconds.</li>
</ol>

static void Adv_Update_Req(void)
{
  /**
   * The code shall be executed in the background as an aci command may be sent
   * The background is the only place where the application can make sure a new aci command
   * is not sent if there is a pending one
   */
  UTIL_SEQ_SetTask(1 << CFG_TASK_ADV_UPDATE_ID, CFG_SCH_PRIO_1);
}

static void Adv_Update(void)
{
  FS_Adv_Request(APP_BLE_LP_ADV);
}

{
  /**
   * For details of Bluetooth advertised local name, see:
   * https://www.bluetooth.com/specifications/css-11/
   */

  const char *name = FS_State_Get()->device_name;
  const size_t name_len = strlen(name);
  uint8_t mfg_data[] = { 4, AD_TYPE_MANUFACTURER_SPECIFIC_DATA, 0xDB, 0x09, 0x00 };
  uint8_t adv_data[31];
  uint8_t k = 0;
  uint8_t ad_length;
  uint8_t ad_type;
  tBleStatus ret;

  if ((NewStatus == APP_BLE_FAST_ADV) || (NewStatus == APP_BLE_LP_ADV))
  {
    /* Set flag in manufacturer specific data */
    mfg_data[4] = request_pairing;

    /* Copy manufacturer specific data */
    memcpy(&(adv_data[k]), mfg_data, sizeof(mfg_data));
    k += sizeof(mfg_data);

    /* Get short local name if needed */
    if (name_len > sizeof(adv_data) - k - 2)
    {
      ad_length = sizeof(adv_data) - k - 2;
      ad_type = AD_TYPE_SHORTENED_LOCAL_NAME;
    }
    else
    {
      ad_length = name_len;
      ad_type = AD_TYPE_COMPLETE_LOCAL_NAME;
    }

    /* Copy local name */
    adv_data[k++] = 1 + ad_length;
    adv_data[k++] = ad_type;
    memcpy(&(adv_data[k]), name, ad_length);
    k += ad_length;

    /* Update advertising data */
    ret = aci_gap_update_adv_data(k, adv_data);
    if (ret != BLE_STATUS_SUCCESS)
    {
      APP_DBG_MSG("==>> aci_gap_update_adv_data - fail, result: 0x%x \n", ret);
    }
    else
    {
      APP_DBG_MSG("==>> aci_gap_update_adv_data - Success\n");
    }
  }
}

**Tool: Bash** — Verify offline whether the recorded private addresses derive from the FlySight's identity key

~~~~bash
cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/rpa_check.py <<'EOF'
"""Check whether BLE resolvable private addresses were generated from the IRK derived from flysight.txt's BLE_IRK (IR root)."""
import itertools, subprocess, sys
IR = bytes.fromhex("5b53109e8e7a6dc45f7a31d1c47dcd62")
def aes(key, pt):
    out = subprocess.run(["openssl","enc","-aes-128-ecb","-nopad","-K",key.hex()], input=pt, capture_output=True).stdout
    assert len(out) == 16, out
    return out
def ah(irk_be, prand_be):            # Core spec: ah(k, r) = e(k, 0-padding || r) mod 2^24
    return aes(irk_be, bytes(13) + prand_be)[13:]
def variants():
    for ir_rev, d_first, irk_rev in itertools.product((0,1),(0,1),(0,1)):
        ir = IR[::-1] if ir_rev else IR
        d = (bytes([1]) + bytes(15)) if d_first else (bytes(15) + bytes([1]))   # d1(IR, d=1, r=0)
        irk = aes(ir, d)
        yield (ir_rev, d_first, irk_rev), (irk[::-1] if irk_rev else irk)
def ok(irk, addr):
    b = bytes.fromhex(addr.replace(":", ""))       # printed MSB first: prand(3) || hash(3)
    return ah(irk, b[:3]) == b[3:]
known = sys.argv[1:]
for name, irk in variants():
    res = [ok(irk, a) for a in known]
    print(name, "IRK", irk.hex(), "".join("Y" if r else "." for r in res))
EOF
~~~~

**Tool: Bash** — Compute the advertising period and phase of each FlySight identifier seen

~~~~bash
cd /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-hozakan-dev-FlySight-flysight-2-firmware--claude-worktrees-repo-status-ebc48f/5c1c2059-49eb-462a-9330-2c1db9a85699/scratchpad/blelab && python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
rows=[]
for l in open("noble.log"):
    m=re.match(r"\[\s*([0-9.]+)\] scan: (.*?)\s+([0-9A-F]{8})-\S+ rssi=(-?\d+) mfg=0xDB09 data=(\w+)",l)
    if m: rows.append((float(m.group(1)),m.group(2).strip(),m.group(3),int(m.group(4))))
P=None
for uid in sorted(set(r[2] for r in rows)):
    ts=sorted(set(r[0] for r in rows if r[2]==uid)); name=[r[1] for r in rows if r[2]==uid][0]
    rs=[r[3] for r in rows if r[2]==uid]
    d=[round(b-a,2) for a,b in zip(ts,ts[1:])]
    # phase on a 1.7555 s grid
    per=1.7555
    ph=[round(t%per,2) for t in ts]
    print(f"{uid} '{name}' n={len(ts)} rssi {min(rs)}..{max(rs)}\n   times {ts}\n   phase(mod {per}) {ph}")
EOF
~~~~

void APP_BLE_RequestPairing(void (*Callback)(void))
{
  /* Prepare for pairing request */
  Next_Adv_Callback = Callback;
  request_pairing = 1;

  /* Request fast advertising */
  FS_Adv_Request(APP_BLE_FAST_ADV);
}

void APP_BLE_CancelPairing(void)
{
  /* Prepare for pairing request */
  Next_Adv_Callback = 0;
  request_pairing = 0;

  if (BleApplicationContext.SmartPhone_Connection_Status == APP_BLE_FAST_ADV)
  {
    /* Request low power advertising */
    FS_Adv_Request(APP_BLE_LP_ADV);
  }
}

Result:

~~~~
#include "main.h"
#include "app_ble.h"
#include "app_common.h"
#include "led.h"
#include "mode.h"

static void FS_PairingMode_Callback(void)
{
	FS_Mode_PushQueue(FS_MODE_EVENT_FORCE_UPDATE);
}

void FS_PairingMode_Init(void)
{
	// Initialize LEDs
	FS_LED_SetColour(FS_LED_GREEN);
	FS_LED_Pulse();

	// Request pairing
	APP_BLE_RequestPairing(FS_PairingMode_Callback);
}

void FS_PairingMode_DeInit(void)
{
	// Turn off LEDs
	FS_LED_Off();

	// Cancel pairing
	APP_BLE_CancelPairing();
}
static FS_Mode_State_t FS_Mode_State_Pairing(FS_Mode_Event_t event)
{
	FS_Mode_State_t next_mode = FS_MODE_STATE_PAIRING;

	if (event == FS_MODE_EVENT_BUTTON_PRESSED)
	{
		FS_PairingMode_DeInit();
		next_mode = FS_MODE_STATE_SLEEP;
	}
	else if (event == FS_MODE_EVENT_FORCE_UPDATE)
	{
		FS_PairingMode_DeInit();
		next_mode = FS_MODE_STATE_SLEEP;
	}

	return next_mode;
}
~~~~

~~~~bash
SCR=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-hozakan-dev-FlySight-flysight-2-firmware--claude-worktrees-repo-status-ebc48f/5c1c2059-49eb-462a-9330-2c1db9a85699/scratchpad; python3 - <<'EOF'

  {
    /* Request low power advertising */
    FS_Adv_Request(APP_BLE_LP_ADV);
  }
}'''
new='''  /*
   * Leave the pairing advertising. When the 30 s window expires, the advertising
   * timer has already restarted advertising in low power mode, still in pairing
   * configuration (pairing flag set, accept list off), before the mode task gets
   * here: restart it in that case too, or it stays that way indefinitely.
   */
  if ((BleApplicationContext.SmartPhone_Connection_Status == APP_BLE_FAST_ADV)
      || (BleApplicationContext.SmartPhone_Connection_Status == APP_BLE_LP_ADV))
  {
    /* Request low power advertising */
    FS_Adv_Request(APP_BLE_LP_ADV);
  }
}'''
assert s.count(old)==1
open(p,"w").write(s.replace(old,new))
EOF
~~~~

~~~~bash
**The user's problem statement (their words, 2026-10-07):** after bonding the FlySight with an Apple device, putting the FlySight back in pairing mode does not work at all; fine on Android. Do not rephrase it as "a paired Mac can never reconnect": the user rejected that wording, even though the measurements below show idle reconnection failing too on this Mac.

**Proven on the bench (macOS 26.3.2, one board):**
- A Mac connects from its *public identity address* (FlySight sees `peer_type=0`, no peer RPA). `ble_count_bonded_devices()` in `STM32_WPAN/App/app_ble.c` puts bonded peers in the resolving list, whose entries default to Network Privacy mode, so the controller silently drops that request: no HCI event at all, in idle *and* in pairing mode. Fix: `hci_le_set_privacy_mode(type, addr, 1)` per bonded entry. Proof is an A/B/A on one boot and one bond, flipping only a RAM byte over SWD: ON works, OFF fails, ON works. Same code on master and in the user's original firmware (7d1f688); resolving-list code dates from 2024.
- Second firmware defect, also upstream since 2024: when the 30 s pairing window times out, the advertising timer restarts advertising still in pairing configuration (flag 01, accept list off) and `APP_BLE_CancelPairing()` only restarted it when the state was FAST_ADV, so it stayed that way forever. Fixed by also restarting when LP_ADV.
- With the Mac bonded, the Mac resolves the FlySight in pairing mode to the *same* identifier as in idle (the id does not change), including after a reboot of the FlySight (new static address each boot, resolution goes through the IRK).
- iOS and Android were never measured. iOS normally connects from an RPA, so the privacy-mode cause may not apply there.

**Why:** earlier work in this session drew wrong conclusions from opaque CoreBluetooth identifiers and mixed firmware/bond states.
~~~~

## Ce qui est prouvé sur macOS

Pour ne plus comparer des firmwares et des liaisons différents, j'ai fait un seul firmware instrumenté où la correction s'active ou se coupe à chaud par SWD. Même démarrage, même liaison avec le Mac, seul un octet en RAM change :

| Correction | Connexion au repos | Connexion en mode pairing | Ce que voit le FlySight |
|---|---|---|---|
| active | OK | OK | connexion du Mac, chiffrement avec la liaison existante |
| coupée (= `master`) | échec (−10) | échec (−10) | aucun événement de connexion |
| réactivée | OK | OK | idem première ligne |

- **Cause** : le Mac se connecte avec son adresse publique fixe. Pour un appareil déjà lié, le contrôleur radio du FlySight n'accepte par défaut qu'une adresse privée tournante et ignore le reste sans rien signaler.
- **Correction** : `hci_le_set_privacy_mode()` pour chaque appareil lié, dans [app_ble.c](STM32_WPAN/App/app_ble.c:1650).
- **Origine** : ce code est identique sur `master` et dans ton firmware d'origine (`7d1f688`), il date de 2024.

## Là où mes mesures contredisent ton énoncé

Sur ce Mac, sans la correction, la connexion échoue **aussi au repos**, pas seulement en mode pairing. Une tentative vers ton vrai « FlySight HozakaN », déjà lié à ce Mac, a expiré de la même façon (un seul essai, signal faible). Je peux te le montrer en direct avec ton application en basculant l'interrupteur.

## Un second défaut du firmware, trouvé et corrigé

Quand la fenêtre de 30 s expire sans connexion, la LED s'éteint mais la publicité repart en configuration « pairing » (drapeau 01, liste d'acceptation désactivée) et y reste indéfiniment. Ce défaut existe sur `master` depuis 2024. Je l'ai corrigé dans `APP_BLE_CancelPairing()` : après expiration, la publicité revient maintenant au repos (vérifié sur la carte).

## L'identifiant qui change

- Une fois le Mac lié, il reconnaît la carte sous **le même identifiant** au repos, en mode pairing et après redémarrage du FlySight.
- Il y a en revanche un **troisième émetteur nommé « FlySight »** à portée du Mac. Avec ma carte totalement muette, il continue d'émettre (−57 à −74 dBm, plus fort que HozakaN). Son identifiant côté Mac change au fil du temps.
- C'est lui que les tests précédents attrapaient par moments. C'est peut-être aussi ce que tu vois comme « l'id qui change » dans une liste de scan.

## Ce que je ne sais pas

Je n'ai rien mesuré sur iOS ni sur Android. iOS se connecte normalement avec une adresse tournante, donc la cause trouvée sur Mac ne s'y applique peut-être pas.

La carte est prête pour le vérifier : firmware instrumenté, liée au Mac, au repos. Peux-tu refaire ton scénario avec l'iPad (appairage, puis mode pairing à nouveau, puis connexion) et me dire quand c'est fait ? Je lirai côté FlySight ce que l'iPad a réellement tenté.

**Tool: Bash** — Correct the code comment and the memory note to match the measured behaviour

~~~~bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
p="STM32_WPAN/App/app_ble.c"
s=open(p).read()
old='''  /*
   * Leave the pairing advertising. When the 30 s window expires, the advertising
   * timer has already restarted advertising in low power mode, still in pairing
   * configuration (pairing flag set, accept list off), before the mode task gets
   * here: restart it in that case too, or it stays that way indefinitely.
   */'''
new='''  /*
   * Leave the pairing advertising. When the 30 s window expires, the advertising
   * timer has already restarted advertising in low power mode, still in pairing
   * configuration (limited discoverable, pairing flag set, accept list off),
   * before the mode task gets here. Restart it in that case too: otherwise the
   * pairing flag stays on air until the stack ends the limited discoverable mode
   * (about 3 minutes later), and then nothing advertises at all until the next
   * button press.
   */'''
~~~~

## Assistant (17:36)

Tu avais raison de douter : mon « indéfiniment » était faux. Je l'avais déduit du code sans l'observer. Voici ce que j'ai mesuré, sur la même carte, en activant ou non la correction à chaud.

## Ce qui se passe après un double appui sans connexion

| | Firmware d'origine | Avec la correction |
|---|---|---|
| 0 à 30 s | drapeau pairing (01) | drapeau pairing (01) |
| 30 s à ~204 s | **toujours drapeau 01**, LED éteinte | publicité normale au repos (00) |
| après ~204 s | **plus aucune annonce** | publicité au repos, qui continue |
| Connexion du Mac lié ensuite | échec (−10) | réussie |

- À 30 s, le minuteur relance la publicité encore en configuration pairing. La sortie de mode (`APP_BLE_CancelPairing()`) ne la relance pas ensuite au repos.
- Vers 204 s, la pile ST met fin d'elle-même au mode « limited discoverable » (événement `0x0400`, non traité). Le FlySight ne s'annonce alors plus du tout.
- Brancher puis débrancher l'USB ne rétablit rien. Seul un nouveau double appui relance la publicité.
- La correction tient en trois lignes dans [app_ble.c](STM32_WPAN/App/app_ble.c:1475). Le défaut est le même sur `master` et dans ton firmware d'origine.

## Lien avec ton problème

Les deux défauts s'enchaînent, sur un Mac déjà lié :

1. Tu repasses le FlySight en mode pairing.
2. La demande de connexion du Mac est ignorée par le contrôleur radio (premier défaut).
3. Aucune connexion n'arrive, donc la fenêtre expire.
4. Environ trois minutes plus tard, le FlySight n'annonce plus rien (second défaut). Plus rien ne peut se connecter, même au repos, jusqu'à un nouveau double appui ou un redémarrage.

C'est cohérent avec ton constat sur Android, où la connexion aboutit pendant la fenêtre, mais je ne l'ai pas mesuré sur Android. Avec les deux corrections, le Mac lié se connecte en mode pairing comme au repos.

## Ce qui reste

- **iOS n'est toujours pas mesuré.** La carte est prête (firmware instrumenté, liée au Mac, au repos). Si tu refais ton scénario avec l'iPad, je lirai côté FlySight ce qu'il a tenté.
- Le renommage est bien visible : il ne reste que ma carte sous le nom « FlySight », donc plus de confusion possible.
- Le rapport HTML est périmé. Je le réécris dès que tu me dis si on attend la mesure iOS ou non.
- Rien n'est commité, et le dépôt ne contient aucun code d'instrumentation.

~~~~bash
"""aui.py dump | tap <text> [n] | shot <file> | wait <text> [seconds]  -- minimal Android UI driver over adb."""
import re, subprocess, sys, time

    return r.stdout if binary else r.stdout.decode(errors="replace")
def nodes():

        t=a.get("text",""); d=a.get("content-desc","")
        if not (t or d): continue
        b=re.match(r"\[(\d+),(\d+)\]\[(\d+),(\d+)\]",a.get("bounds",""))
        if not b: continue
        x0,y0,x1,y1=map(int,b.groups())
        out.append((t,d,(x0+x1)//2,(y0+y1)//2,a.get("package","")))
    return out
def dump():
    for t,d,x,y,p in nodes(): print(f"({x:4d},{y:4d}) {t!r}"+(f" desc={d!r}" if d else "")+(f"  [{p}]" if p and "skygames" not in p else ""))
cmd=sys.argv[1]
if cmd=="dump": dump()
elif cmd=="tap":
    want=sys.argv[2].lower(); idx=int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv)>3 else 0
    hits=[n for n in nodes() if want in n[0].lower() or want in n[1].lower()]
    if len(hits)<=idx: print("NOT FOUND:",sys.argv[2]); sys.exit(1)
    t,d,x,y,p=hits[idx]; sh("shell","input","tap",str(x),str(y)); print(f"tapped {t or d!r} at ({x},{y})")
elif cmd=="wait":
    want=sys.argv[2].lower(); end=time.time()+float(sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv)>3 else 15)
    while time.time()<end:
        if any(want in n[0].lower() or want in n[1].lower() for n in nodes()): print("seen:",sys.argv[2]); sys.exit(0)
        time.sleep(0.7)
    print("TIMEOUT waiting for",sys.argv[2]); sys.exit(1)
elif cmd=="shot":
    open(sys.argv[2],"wb").write(sh("exec-out","screencap","-p",binary=True)); print("saved",sys.argv[2])
~~~~

**Tool: Bash** — Tap the exact FlySight entry and follow the app and the FlySight timeline

~~~~bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
p="/private/tmp/claude-501/aui.py"; s=open(p).read()
old='''    hits=[n for n in nodes() if want in n[0].lower() or want in n[1].lower()]
    if len(hits)<=idx: print("NOT FOUND:",sys.argv[2]); sys.exit(1)'''
new='''    ns=nodes()
    hits=[n for n in ns if want==n[0].lower() or want==n[1].lower()] or [n for n in ns if want in n[0].lower() or want in n[1].lower()]
    if len(hits)<=idx: print("NOT FOUND:",sys.argv[2]); sys.exit(1)'''
assert old in s; open(p,"w").write(s.replace(old,new))
EOF
A=/private/tmp/claude-501/aui.py; D=/private/tmp/claude-501/dbg2.py; ADB=~/Library/Android/sdk/platform-tools/adb; M=$(python3 $D mark); $ADB logcat -c; python3 $A tap "FlySight"; for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do sleep 3; python3 $A dump 2>/dev/null | head -8 | tr '\n' ';' | cut -c1-260; echo; done; echo "--- côté FlySight:"; python3 $D read --since $M
~~~~

~~~~bash
<h1>FlySight 2: pairing mode stops working once a Mac is bonded</h1>
<div class="meta">Findings and fixes &middot; 7 October 2026 &middot; firmware branch <code>claude/repo-status-ebc48f</code> (on top of <code>origin/master</code>) &middot; this version replaces an earlier draft whose problem statement was wrong</div>

<div class="callout tldr">
<p><strong>Summary.</strong></p>
<ul>
  <li><strong>Reported problem.</strong> After a FlySight 2 has been bonded with an Apple device, putting the FlySight back in pairing mode does not work at all. The same flow works on Android.</li>
  <li><strong>Cause 1 (measured on macOS).</strong> A Mac connects from its fixed public address. For an already bonded peer, the FlySight's radio controller only accepts a rotating private address, and drops anything else without telling the firmware. An Android phone connects from a rotating private address, so it is accepted.</li>
  <li><strong>Cause 2 (measured, any platform).</strong> When a 30-second pairing window ends without a connection, the FlySight keeps advertising "pairing" for about 204 seconds, then stops advertising completely until the button is pressed again.</li>
  <li><strong>Together.</strong> The bonded Mac cannot connect during the pairing window (cause 1), so the window times out, so the FlySight goes silent (cause 2). Nothing can connect any more.</li>
  <li><strong>Fixes.</strong> Two small changes in <code>STM32_WPAN/App/app_ble.c</code>. With both, the Mac and the Android phone connect in pairing mode and in idle. <strong>iOS was not measured.</strong></li>
</ul>
</div>
~~~~

## Assistant (18:57)

Les tests Android sont faits : ton flux fonctionne bien sur Android avec le firmware d'origine, et la mesure montre pourquoi le Mac échoue là où le téléphone passe.

## Ce que voit le FlySight à la connexion

```
Mac      : peer=FC:B2:14:…  (adresse publique)            peerRPA=none
Android  : peer=64:9D:38:…  (identité, résolue)           peerRPA=75:D8:EE:25:A8:07
```

- Le téléphone se présente avec une adresse privée tournante, que le FlySight rattache à sa liaison : accepté.
- Le Mac se présente avec son adresse publique nue : ignoré par le contrôleur radio pour un appareil déjà lié.

## Résultats sur le Pixel (SkyGames 1.0.0-RC2, piloté par adb)

| Scénario | Firmware d'origine | Avec les deux corrections |
|---|---|---|
| Appairage en mode pairing | OK | non refait (liaison conservée) |
| Mode pairing à nouveau, reconnexion | OK, configuration chargée | OK |
| Reconnexion au repos | non testé | OK |
| Mac, carte liée au Mac et au téléphone | non retesté | OK au repos et en mode pairing |

Les corrections ne cassent donc rien sur Android.

## Deux choses apprises en route

- **Liaison obsolète** : le téléphone gardait une ancienne liaison avec ma carte. Android détecte la clé manquante et relance tout seul un appairage, sous forme de notification à valider en moins de 30 s. macOS, lui, échoue et impose d'oublier l'appareil.
- **Ma première tentative a échoué par ma faute** : mon automatisation a validé la notification pile à l'expiration des 30 s. La suivante, plus rapide, a réussi.

## Rapport

Je l'ai réécrit sur ces faits : [Docs/ble-pairing-after-bond-report.html](Docs/ble-pairing-after-bond-report.html). L'ancien fichier, faux dès le premier paragraphe, est supprimé. Une précision : « LED éteinte » y vient de l'état interne du firmware, je n'ai pas regardé la LED.

## État laissé

- **Téléphone** : l'application a maintenant une tuile « FlySight » pour ma carte de test, créée par mon essai. J'ai accepté une demande d'association Android, sans cocher l'accès aux contacts.
- **Carte** : firmware instrumenté, les deux corrections actives, liée au Mac et au téléphone.
- **Dépôts** : rien n'est commité, aucun code d'instrumentation dedans.

Il reste iOS, jamais mesuré. Veux-tu faire l'essai avec l'iPad pendant que je lis côté FlySight, ou préfères-tu que je commite d'abord les corrections ?

~~~~bash
  return (int8_t)total;''','''  // 4) Let bonded peers connect with their identity address too. Entries of the
  //    resolving list default to Network Privacy mode, where the controller
  //    silently ignores a connection request that does not use a resolvable
  //    private address. A Mac connects from its public identity address
  //    (measured on macOS 26), so without this a bonded Mac never reaches us,
  //    in pairing mode or not.
  for (uint8_t k = 0; k < total; k++)
  {
    ret = hci_le_set_privacy_mode(rl_entries[k].Peer_Identity_Address_Type,
                                  rl_entries[k].Peer_Identity_Address,
                                  BLE_PRIVACY_MODE_DEVICE);
    if (ret != BLE_STATUS_SUCCESS)
    {
      APP_DBG_MSG("hci_le_set_privacy_mode fail %x\\r\\n", ret);
    }
  }

  APP_DBG_MSG("Resolving List populated with %u bonded device(s)\\r\\n", total);
  return (int8_t)total;''')
rep('''  if (BleApplicationContext.Device_Connection_Status == APP_BLE_FAST_ADV)
  {
    /* Request low power advertising */
    FS_Adv_Request(APP_BLE_LP_ADV);
  }
}''','''  /*
   * Leave the pairing advertising. When the 30 s window expires, the advertising
   * timer has already restarted advertising in low power mode, still in pairing
   * configuration (limited discoverable, pairing flag set, accept list off),
   * before the mode task gets here. Restart it in that case too: otherwise the
   * pairing flag stays on air until the stack ends the limited discoverable mode
   * (about 3 minutes later), and then nothing advertises at all until the next
   * button press.
   */
  if ((BleApplicationContext.Device_Connection_Status == APP_BLE_FAST_ADV)
      || (BleApplicationContext.Device_Connection_Status == APP_BLE_LP_ADV))

    FS_Adv_Request(APP_BLE_LP_ADV);

}''')
~~~~
