**Tool: Bash** — Read the earlier boot HardFault fix carried by the branch

~~~~bash
git show --stat --format='%h %s%n%n%b' 89d5e1c | head -30; git show 89d5e1c -- STM32_WPAN/App/ble_tx_queue.c | sed -n 1,60p
~~~~
Result:

~~~~
89d5e1c Fix HardFault at boot when USB is plugged in

While start-up waits for CPU2, the sequencer runs every pending task. With
VBUS present at boot, FS_Mode_Update is pending and calls Custom_Mode_Update,
which queued a BLE packet and set the BLE TX queue task before
BLE_TX_Queue_Init() had registered it. The sequencer then called a NULL
callback (HardFault, INVSTATE).

Only schedule the transmit task once it is registered, keep packets queued
before that, and send them from BLE_TX_Queue_Init() so the Mode
characteristic still reflects the current mode.


 STM32_WPAN/App/ble_tx_queue.c | 30 +++++++++++++++++++++++++-----
 1 file changed, 25 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)
commit 89d5e1cf7535325688b4932825a618fa17865d9e
Author: Guillaume Imbert <guillaume.m.imbert@gmail.com>
Date:   Wed Oct 7 05:48:21 2026 +0200

    Fix HardFault at boot when USB is plugged in
    
    While start-up waits for CPU2, the sequencer runs every pending task. With
    VBUS present at boot, FS_Mode_Update is pending and calls Custom_Mode_Update,
    which queued a BLE packet and set the BLE TX queue task before
    BLE_TX_Queue_Init() had registered it. The sequencer then called a NULL
    callback (HardFault, INVSTATE).
    
    Only schedule the transmit task once it is registered, keep packets queued
    before that, and send them from BLE_TX_Queue_Init() so the Mode
    characteristic still reflects the current mode.

diff --git a/STM32_WPAN/App/ble_tx_queue.c b/STM32_WPAN/App/ble_tx_queue.c
index c88da17..4317871 100644
--- a/STM32_WPAN/App/ble_tx_queue.c
+++ b/STM32_WPAN/App/ble_tx_queue.c
@@ -41,23 +41,43 @@ typedef struct
 static BLE_TX_Queue_Packet_t tx_buffer[FS_CRS_WINDOW_LENGTH+1];
 static uint32_t tx_read_index, tx_write_index;
 static uint8_t tx_flow_status;
+static uint8_t tx_ready;
 
 static void BLE_TX_Queue_Transmit(void);
 
+/*
+ * While start-up waits for CPU2 the sequencer runs every pending task, so
+ * application code (e.g. a mode change when USB is plugged in at boot) can
+ * queue packets before BLE_TX_Queue_Init() has registered the transmit task.
+ * Setting an unregistered task makes the sequencer call a NULL callback, so
+ * only schedule once registered; BLE_TX_Queue_Init() sends what is waiting.
+ */
+static void BLE_TX_Queue_Schedule(void)
+{
+	if (tx_ready)
+	{
+		UTIL_SEQ_SetTask(1<<CFG_TASK_BLE_TX_QUEUE_TRANSMIT_ID, CFG_SCH_PRIO_1);
+	}
+}
+
 void BLE_TX_Queue_Init(void)
 {
-	tx_read_index = 0;
-	tx_write_index = 0;
 	tx_flow_status = 1;
 
 	UTIL_SEQ_RegTask(1<<CFG_TASK_BLE_TX_QUEUE_TRANSMIT_ID, UTIL_SEQ_RFU,
 			BLE_TX_Queue_Transmit);
+	tx_ready = 1;
+
+	if (tx_read_index < tx_write_index)
+	{
+		BLE_TX_Queue_Schedule();
+	}
 }
 
 void BLE_TX_Queue_TxPoolAvailableNotification(void)
~~~~

<h1>FlySight 2 firmware: three BLE fixes proposed for merge</h1>
<div class="meta">Prepared by Guillaume Imbert &middot; 7 October 2026 &middot; checked against <code>origin/master</code> (<code>9ec7186</code>) and <code>origin/develop</code> (<code>e67ee9f</code>). The same patch applies to both.</div>

<p>While using a FlySight 2 with a Mac, one symptom kept coming back: <strong>once the FlySight has been bonded with the Mac, putting it back in pairing mode does not work, and the Mac cannot connect any more. The same sequence works from an Android phone.</strong> Tracking it down on a bench led to two causes in the firmware, plus a third, unrelated defect found on the way. This document describes each one and the change proposed for it.</p>

<table>
  <tr><th>#</th><th>Bug</th><th>Seen on</th><th>Proposed change</th></tr>
  <tr><td>1</td><td>A Mac that is already bonded can no longer connect, in pairing mode or idle</td><td><code>master</code>, <code>develop</code></td><td><code>app_ble.c</code>, <code>ble_count_bonded_devices()</code>: one call per bonded device</td></tr>
  <tr><td>2</td><td>A pairing window that expires unused leaves the FlySight advertising "pairing" for about 3.5 minutes, then not advertising at all</td><td><code>develop</code> (latent on <code>master</code>)</td><td><code>app_ble.c</code>, <code>Adv_Update()</code>: one statement</td></tr>
  <tr><td>3</td><td>The BLE keys are all zero on a first boot without <code>flysight.txt</code></td><td><code>master</code>, <code>develop</code></td><td><code>state.c</code>, <code>FS_State_Read()</code>: no early return before the keys are generated</td></tr>
</table>
<p>Bugs 1 and 2 chain into the reported symptom on <code>develop</code>: the bonded Mac cannot connect during the pairing window (bug 1), so the window expires unused, so the FlySight ends up silent (bug 2). Test results for all three are in <a href="#tests">section 4</a>, the complete patch in <a href="#patch">section 5</a>.</p>

When the 30 s window times out without a connection, `Adv_Update()` restarts advertising while `request_pairing` is still 1 (limited discoverable, flag 01, accept list off), and `APP_BLE_CancelPairing()` then does not restart it. Measured where it shows: flag 01 for about 205 s, then the stack raises `ACI_GAP_LIMITED_DISCOVERABLE` timeout (0x0400, not handled) and the FlySight stops advertising; USB replug does not help, a new double press does.
- **Where it shows matters:** only when `CFG_TASK_FS_MODE_UPDATE_ID` is in the "with HCI command" task list: `origin/develop` since upstream commit 7b57cc8 (2026-07-13) and this branch since aac9740. I first claimed "same on master" from reading the code; the control run disproved it. Run the control on the exact base before claiming scope.
- **Fix kept:** `request_pairing = 0;` at the top of `Adv_Update()`. Correct on both branches. The earlier variant (restart from `APP_BLE_CancelPairing()` when LP_ADV) was dropped: on master that function can run while another HCI command is pending.
- The two defects chain on a bonded Mac on develop: its connection is dropped (first defect), so the window times out, so the FlySight ends up silent (second defect). On Android the connection succeeds inside the window.

'''

Le rapport pour le créateur du FlySight est prêt, mais d'abord une erreur de ma part sur ton téléphone : **tu es très probablement déconnecté de ton compte dans SkyGames**.

## Ce qui s'est passé sur le téléphone

- Mon script cherchait le bouton « Déconnecter » (la liaison BLE) en acceptant les libellés approchants. Il a très probablement touché « Se déconnecter » sur l'écran d'erreur de compte de SkyGames.
- En cherchant ensuite « Connecter », il a touché « Se connecter avec Apple », ce qui a ouvert la page de connexion Apple dans Chrome.
- Je n'ai rien saisi. Je suis revenu en arrière et l'application est sur son écran de connexion. Tu devras te reconnecter.
- Je n'ai plus touché au téléphone depuis, et mon outil n'accepte plus que des libellés exacts.

## Le rapport

[Docs/ble-pairing-fixes-report.html](Docs/ble-pairing-fixes-report.html), en anglais, trois bugs traités chacun en Glossary > Problem > Proposed fix, puis les tests et le correctif complet. L'ancien rapport est supprimé. Je n'ai pas pu revérifier le rendu en largeur réduite, le panneau du navigateur étant masqué.

## Ce que la préparation du rapport a changé

Pour décrire le code que le mainteneur aura sous les yeux, j'ai testé sur `origin/master` et `origin/develop`, et pas seulement sur ta branche. Deux de mes affirmations précédentes étaient fausses :

- **Le second bug n'apparaît pas sur `master`.** Il n'apparaît que sur `develop`, depuis le commit `7b57cc8` de Michael Cooper (13 juillet 2026), qui a reclassé la tâche des modes. Sur `master`, un hasard d'ordonnancement le masque.
- **Ma première correction de ce bug était dangereuse sur `master`.** Je l'ai remplacée par une ligne dans `Adv_Update()`, sûre sur les deux branches. Ta branche contient maintenant cette version.

Résultats côté Mac, sur la carte :

| Firmware | Mac au repos | Mac en mode pairing | Fenêtre pairing expirée |
|---|---|---|---|
| `master` non modifié | échec | échec | correct |
| `master` + correctif | OK | OK | correct |
| `develop` non modifié | échec | échec | « pairing » pendant 205 s, puis silence |
| `develop` + correctif | OK | OK | correct |

Le correctif est identique pour les deux branches : 2 fichiers, 54 lignes ajoutées, 16 retirées.

## À savoir avant de l'envoyer

- **iOS n'est toujours pas testé**, et le rapport le dit.
- **Android n'a pas été rejoué sur les firmwares corrigés finaux.** Il l'a été sur `develop` non modifié et sur le firmware instrumenté.
- **`origin/develop` ne démarre pas sur mon banc** quand l'USB est branché à la mise sous tension (HardFault). Ta branche contient déjà le correctif (`89d5e1c`). Le rapport le signale comme un problème séparé.
- Le rapport est signé de ton nom. Rien n'est commité.

La carte tourne sur ta branche avec les corrections finales, branchée en USB.

<p><strong>Why step 3 happens in practice.</strong> Users start a new pairing to make the FlySight advertise again when it has stopped advertising. Bug 2 below is one way the FlySight ends up not advertising.</p>
<p><strong>The starting hypothesis.</strong> Apple platforms never show an app the FlySight's address, only an opaque identifier. The suspicion was that, once the FlySight restarts pairing, the host can no longer map it to the device it bonded with.</p>

<h2 id="found">What the investigation found</h2>
<ul>
  <li><strong>The hypothesis was not confirmed on macOS.</strong> Once bonded, the Mac shows the FlySight under one and the same identifier when it is idle, when it is back in pairing mode, and after the FlySight reboots. So the host does find the FlySight. What fails is the connection itself: the Mac's connection request is discarded by the FlySight's radio controller before the firmware hears of it (<a href="#b1">bug 1</a>).</li>
  <li><strong>Android is not affected</strong> because it connects in a different way, which the controller accepts. The difference between the platforms is in the address the <em>host</em> connects from, not in how it identifies the FlySight.</li>
  <li><strong>A FlySight that stops advertising</strong> was reproduced on <code>develop</code>: a pairing window that expires unused ends with no advertising at all (<a href="#b2">bug 2</a>). On <code>develop</code> the two chain: the bonded Mac cannot connect during the window, the window expires unused, and the FlySight goes silent.</li>
  <li><strong>iOS was not measured.</strong> Whether an iPhone or iPad fails for the same reason as the Mac, or for the identifier reason, is still open.</li>
  <li>A third, unrelated defect was found on the way (<a href="#b3">bug 3</a>).</li>
</ul>

~~~~
# haiOS Probe

haiOS's own agent on an appliance. It is what lets haiOS **tap, swipe, type and take a
picture** on a physical Apple device — the two things Apple's own tools do not offer.

**Not only iOS.** A Linux, Windows or macOS test machine has neither adb nor usbmux, so a
probe is the common mechanism and iOS is merely the first place Apple makes it
compulsory. That is why this is a Kotlin Multiplatform project and not an Xcode one.

## Why it has to exist at all

`xcrun devicectl` installs, launches, stops and lists. It does not inject a touch, and no
tool does: **Apple offers no key or touch injection on a physical device from the host.**
Since iOS 17 it does not offer a screenshot either — `com.apple.mobile.screenshotr` answers
`InvalidService`, because the developer services moved onto RemoteXPC behind a tunnel whose
creation needs root.

So both input and capture come from something running *on* the appliance. That is this.

## Why the iOS half must be a XCUITest target and not an app

An ordinary iOS app is in a sandbox: it can draw in its own window and touch nothing else.
It could not tap a button in Réglages if it wanted to.

A **XCUITest runner** can, because `testmanagerd` hands it automation privileges when it
starts it. That is the same mechanism Appium's WebDriverAgent uses — its own documentation
says it "works by linking `XCTest.framework`".

The consequence is that the runner **does not start the way an app starts**:

```
xcodebuild test-without-building -xctestrun <path> -destination 'id=<udid>'
```

`devicectl` has no XCTest path at all — measured against Xcode 26.6, `devicectl device
install` has one subcommand (`app`) and `device process launch` takes a bundle id with no
test option. Launching the runner by its bundle id gives a process with no test session: it
comes up, does nothing, and leaves. And that command **does not return** — the runner lives
for the whole session, so haiOS supervises it as a long-lived child.

## Why the runner is Swift in a Kotlin project

A fair question, and the answer is narrower than "Kotlin cannot".

XCTest is an **Objective-C** framework, and Kotlin/Native has Objective-C interop: it consumes
Objective-C classes, subclasses them, and exports Kotlin classes back to the Objective-C
runtime. Nothing about the language forbids writing an `XCTestCase` in Kotlin.

What forbids it in practice, checked against the Kotlin/Native 2.4.10 toolchain on this
machine:

- XCTest is **not** among Kotlin/Native's 177 shipped platform libraries, and appears nowhere
  in the distribution.
- Kotlin/Native does not run its own tests on iOS out of the box.
- Reaching XCTest through `cinterop` has been tried and is known to fail at link time —
  [kotlin-native#3165](https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin-native/issues/3165) and
  [#3232](https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin-native/issues/3232).
- Gradle's own XCTest support is `SwiftXCTestBundle`: Swift, by name.

So Swift is **the supported path**, not the only conceivable one. If that changes, the split
below is the only thing that would move — and it is one file.

The split itself is worth stating plainly, because it is what keeps the Swift half small:

## What a person does, and what they never do again

Once: install both bundles, open haiOS Companion so it writes a secret, and allow screen
recording the first time iOS asks.

After that, nothing. iOS insists a broadcast is started by somebody choosing to — and the
runner, holding automation privileges, is allowed to be that somebody. It opens the Companion,
taps the picker and taps what the system offers. Closing the last panel stops it again,
because a broadcast outlives everything on the host by design.

 * **This file is one half of a pair.** The other is `crates/haios-core/src/probe.rs` in

 * It lives in Kotlin rather than Swift because the probe is not only iOS. A Linux, Windows or

 * desktop probe and the XCUITest runner; two would agree until somebody edited one.
 *
 * ## The secret is the first line
 *
 * A framed message is the secret, a newline, then a JSON body. The secret is compared
 * **before the body is looked at**: a probe that parses first has already done work for
 * an unauthenticated caller, and on a desktop that caller is anybody who can open a socket.
 *
 * On iOS today the transport is USB, so reaching the probe means being the machine at the end
 * of the cable and none of this can be exploited. That is exactly why it is written now: it
 * is the only moment where it can be got right without a mistake costing anything.
 */

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - FlySight 2 firmware: STM32WB5MMG, ST BLE stack on CPU2 (ACI/HCI), sequencer tasks split into `CFG_Task_Id_With_HCI_Cmd_t` (paused by `BLE_StatusNot` while an HCI command is pending) and `CFG_Task_Id_With_NO_HCI_Cmd_t` (keep running, can run nested inside an HCI wait).
   - BLE privacy: identity address vs resolvable private address (RPA), IRK, bonding, filter accept list (`aci_gap_configure_whitelist`), resolving list (`aci_gap_add_devices_to_resolving_list`), **Network Privacy vs Device Privacy** mode (`hci_le_set_privacy_mode(type, addr, 0x01)`), limited discoverable mode (stack timeout ≈180 s, event `ACI_GAP_LIMITED_DISCOVERABLE_VSEVT_CODE` 0x0400, not handled by the app).
   - Pairing mode: double press → `APP_BLE_RequestPairing` → `request_pairing = 1`, FAST adv 30 s (flag byte 01, `aci_gap_set_limited_discoverable`, no accept list); timer → `Adv_Update()` → `FS_Adv_Request(APP_BLE_LP_ADV)`; mode exit via `FS_PairingMode_Callback` → queued `FS_MODE_EVENT_FORCE_UPDATE` → `FS_PairingMode_DeInit` → `APP_BLE_CancelPairing`.
   - Measured facts: macOS (26.3.2) connects from its **public identity address** (`peer_type=0 peer=FC:B2:14:DB:73:11 peerRPA=none`); Android connects from an RPA resolved by the FlySight (`peer=64:9D:38:D3:8A:34 (public identity (resolved)) peerRPA=75:D8:EE:25:A8:07`). Once bonded, the Mac shows the board under one stable identifier (`6DFDC91D-D47F-C77F-0F68-DA2AF2C204E3`) in idle, in pairing mode and across FlySight reboots (the FlySight's random static address changes every boot; resolution goes through the IRK).
   - Offline IRK check: IRK = AES(key = IR reversed, plaintext 00..01) = `22949b6ac4aed36d8e5d792b25d60514` for `BLE_IRK 5b53109e8e7a6dc45f7a31d1c47dcd62`; an RPA is valid if AES(IRK, 13 zero bytes || prand)[13:] == low 3 bytes (8/8 recorded RPAs verified).
   - Android: stale bond → "key missing" → "Initiating autonomous repairing" → pairing *notification* ("Demande d'association" / "Associer et connecter", then dialog "Associer") that must be accepted within the 30 s SMP timeout (`SMP_CONN_TOUT`). macOS: stale bond → `CBErrorEncryptionTimedOut` (15), FlySight side `DISCONNECTED 0x3d` (MIC failure).
   - SkyGames macOS stack: Compose Desktop + JNA + `libflysight_ble.dylib` (`ble_macos.m`, CoreBluetooth); BleProbe.app test harness built from the same native source.
   - Upstream topology: `origin` = `https://github.com/flysight/flysight-2-firmware.git` (official), `mike` = `crwper/flysight-2-firmware` (Michael Cooper), `perso` = `HozakaN/flysight-2-firmware`. `origin/master` = `9ec7186` (2026-09-09), `origin/develop` = `e67ee9f` (2026-09-09, 97 commits ahead of master, master is an ancestor). The user's branch is NOT based on origin/develop (it is Michael Cooper's v2026.02.13.develop-era work rebased on master + 7 commits by "Guillaume Imbert" from this session: 89d5e1c boot HardFault fix in `ble_tx_queue.c`, aac9740 "Run FS_Mode_Update with the HCI command tasks", 984f4b2, 77c065e, bf75553, dab59f0, cea07c5).
   - haiOS probe (for driving the iPad): XCUITest runner `HaiOSProbeUITests` listening on TCP 7654 on the device; message = `<secret>\n<JSON body>`; actions `{"action":"tap","x":..,"y":..}`, `swipe` (`from_x,from_y,to_x,to_y,ms`), `text`, `key` (`name`, e.g. "home"), `screenshot`, `tree` (`bundle_id`), `broadcast`, `rotate`, `screen`; replies `{"result":"ok"}`, `{"result":"tree","tree":"..."}`, `{"result":"screenshot","png_base64":"..."}`, `{"result":"failed","why":"..."}`, each followed by newline; wrong secret → silence + closed socket. Launched with `TEST_RUNNER_HAIOS_SECRET=<secret> xcodebuild test-without-building -xctestrun <path> -destination 'id=<udid>'` (long-lived, does not return; env optional `HAIOS_PORT`). Reached through usbmux port relay (`usbmux:<udid>:7654`; usbmux needs the device **SerialNumber** UDID like `00008027-0014…`, not the CoreDevice UUID). Tap coordinates are in Springboard's frame (whole screen).

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **`STM32_WPAN/App/app_ble.c`** (firmware working tree, uncommitted) — final state of the two BLE fixes (identical hunks apply to origin/master and origin/develop):
     ```c
     #define BD_ADDR_SIZE_LOCAL    6

     #define BLE_PRIVACY_MODE_DEVICE   0x01 /**< Peer may use its identity address too */
     ```
     ```c
     static void Adv_Update(void)
     {
       /*
        * The fast advertising period is over, and with it any pairing window. The
        * mode task has not left pairing mode yet at this point, so clear the request
        * here: otherwise advertising restarts in pairing configuration (limited
        * discoverable, pairing flag set, accept list off) and nothing restarts it in
        * normal configuration afterwards.
        */
       request_pairing = 0;

       FS_Adv_Request(APP_BLE_LP_ADV);
     }
     ```
     ```c
       // (in ble_count_bonded_devices(), after aci_gap_add_devices_to_resolving_list succeeded)
       // 4) Let bonded peers connect with their identity address too. Entries of the
       //    resolving list default to Network Privacy mode, where the controller
       //    silently ignores a connection request that does not use a resolvable
       //    private address. A Mac connects from its public identity address
       //    (measured on macOS 26), so without this a bonded Mac never reaches us,
       //    in pairing mode or not.
       for (uint8_t k = 0; k < total; k++)
       {
         ret = hci_le_set_privacy_mode(rl_entries[k].Peer_Identity_Address_Type,
                                       rl_entries[k].Peer_Identity_Address,
                                       BLE_PRIVACY_MODE_DEVICE);
         if (ret != BLE_STATUS_SUCCESS)
         {
           APP_DBG_MSG("hci_le_set_privacy_mode fail %x\r\n", ret);
         }
       }
     ```

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Wrong claim "bonded Mac can never reconnect" as the headline** — user: "Dès le départ c'est faux". Measurements do show idle failing too on this Mac, but the problem statement must be the user's (pairing mode after bond). Report rewritten around their statement.
   - **"Another FlySight nearby" theory** — user first said they had only one "FlySight"; proven by silencing the board (`Enable_BLE: 0` + reset) that a third advertiser named "FlySight" existed (three distinct stable advertising phases); user confirmed and renamed it "FlySight Nabil". Lesson: never select the board by name; use pairing flag or bonded identifier.
   - **Second bug claimed as "stays in pairing mode indefinitely" without observation** — user: "Je ne pense pas que ça soit vrai". Measured: flag 01 for ≈204 s, then no advertising; USB replug doesn't restore; new double press does.
   - **Second bug claimed "same on master"** — the control run on unmodified master disproved it (flag 00 at 30 s). Cause: `CFG_TASK_FS_MODE_UPDATE_ID` is in the NO_HCI list on master (runs nested, masks the bug); in the HCI list on develop since upstream commit `7b57cc8` (2026-07-13, "Classify mode update task as using HCI") and on the branch since `aac9740`.
   - **First fix for bug 2 (restart from `APP_BLE_CancelPairing` when LP_ADV)** — dangerous on master (function can run while another HCI command is pending). Replaced by `request_pairing = 0;` in `Adv_Update()`; verified on master and develop.
   - **Master test invalid (probe read `DS_Mode`, absent on master → −13)** — probe now reads `FT_Packet_In`.
   - **Control run invalid: ST-Link dropped after flash / master can hang on simulated unplug** — test scripts now verify "left USB mode : <n>" and retry with reset-probe/reset.
   - **`origin/develop` HardFaults at boot with USB connected (INVSTATE)** — added the branch's boot fix `89d5e1c` (`ble_tx_queue.c`) to the develop bench builds only (documented as a separate issue); with the cable physically unplugged, strictly unmodified develop boots fine (current run).
   - **Android pairing accepted too late (exactly at the 30 s SMP timeout)** — redone faster, succeeded.
   - **Phone incident (my error):** substring matching in `aui.py` most likely tapped "Se déconnecter" (signed the user out of SkyGames) and then tapped "Se connecter avec Apple" (opened Apple sign-in in Chrome); backed out with BACK, nothing typed; user later signed in again. Fixed: exact labels only, package allow-list, foreground and account-screen guards. Also at one point the phone showed Instagram while a script ran.

5. Problem Solving:
   - **Solved/proven (macOS):** Bug 1 — bonded Mac's connection request silently dropped (Network Privacy mode of resolving-list entries); fix = `hci_le_set_privacy_mode(..., device)` per bonded entry. A/B/A on one boot and bond with a RAM switch; and control vs patched on both origin/master and origin/develop.
   - **Solved/proven:** Bug 2 — unused pairing window ends in ~3.5 min of "pairing" advertising then silence, on develop-class firmware; fix in `Adv_Update()`.
   - **Solved:** Bug 3 — all-zero BLE keys without `flysight.txt`.
   - **Test matrix so far (USB cable connected, simulated unplug):**
     - master unmodified: Mac idle FAIL, Mac pairing FAIL, window expiry OK (01 30 s → 00, still advertising at 249 s), Android pairing+idle connected.
     - master + patch: Mac idle OK, pairing OK, window OK (still advertising 247 s), Android connected both.
     - develop unmodified (+boot fix): Mac FAIL/FAIL, window: 01 for 205 s then no advertising, Android connected both.
     - develop + patch (+boot fix): Mac OK/OK, window 01 30 s → 00 (still advertising 242 s), Android connected both.
     - Both patched builds compile with no new warnings (master 11→11, develop 22→22).
   - **In progress:** cable-unplugged (ST-Link only) verification; interim on strictly unmodified develop: boots with no fault, advertises flag 00, Mac idle connect status −10.
   - **Open:** iOS behaviour never measured (user's hypothesis about identifier remapping untested on iOS; not confirmed on macOS). Whether other paths make the FlySight stop advertising in the field is not established beyond bug 2.

/// `xcodebuild test-without-building`, pointed at one appliance and one test.
///
/// Pure, so the shape is checked the way every `*_argv` in this repository is checked: what
/// comes from outside is an argument and never a fragment of a command line.
pub fn launch_argv(xctestrun: &Path, udid: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    vec![
        "xcodebuild".to_string(),
        "test-without-building".to_string(),
        "-xctestrun".to_string(),
        xctestrun.display().to_string(),
        "-destination".to_string(),
        format!("id={udid}"),
        "-only-testing:".to_string() + SERVE,
        // **XCTest kills a test that runs too long, and this one runs until told to stop.**
        // Said here rather than relied on from the `.xctestrun`: that file carries a
        // `TestTimeoutsEnabled` of its own, set by whichever scheme the operator built from,
        // and a probe whose lifetime depends on somebody else's scheme setting is a probe
        // that dies mid-session on one machine and not another.
        "-test-timeouts-enabled".to_string(),
        "NO".to_string(),
    ]
}

"""Temporary instrumentation of app_ble.c (never commit): a timeline of advertising starts and BLE
events readable over SWD, and a RAM switch to turn the Device Privacy fix on/off without reflashing."""
p = "STM32_WPAN/App/app_ble.c"
s = open(p).read()

def rep(old, new, count=1):
    global s
    assert s.count(old) == count, (s.count(old), old[:70])
    s = s.replace(old, new)

rep("static BleApplicationContext_t BleApplicationContext;\n", '''static BleApplicationContext_t BleApplicationContext;

/* TEMP-DBG ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
typedef struct { uint32_t tick; uint8_t kind, a, b, c; uint8_t data[24]; } dbg_rec_t;
volatile dbg_rec_t dbg_log[64];
volatile uint32_t dbg_n;
volatile uint32_t dbg_gatt_n;
volatile uint8_t dbg_use_device_privacy = 1;   /* written over SWD: 0 = behave like master */
volatile uint8_t dbg_use_cancel_fix = 1;       /* written over SWD: 0 = pairing timeout as on master */
volatile uint8_t dbg_bonded, dbg_rl0_type, dbg_rl0_addr[6], dbg_pm_status;
static void dbg_rec(uint8_t kind, uint8_t a, uint8_t b, uint8_t c, const uint8_t *data, uint8_t len)
{
  volatile dbg_rec_t *r = &dbg_log[dbg_n & 63];
  r->tick = HAL_GetTick(); r->kind = kind; r->a = a; r->b = b; r->c = c;
  for (uint8_t i = 0; i < 24; i++) r->data[i] = (data && i < len) ? data[i] : 0;
  dbg_n++;
}
/* --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
''')

rep("  p_event_pckt = (hci_event_pckt*) ((hci_uart_pckt *) p_Pckt)->data;\n\n  switch (p_event_pckt->evt)",
'''  p_event_pckt = (hci_event_pckt*) ((hci_uart_pckt *) p_Pckt)->data;

  /* TEMP-DBG */
  if (p_event_pckt->evt == HCI_DISCONNECTION_COMPLETE_EVT_CODE)
  {
    hci_disconnection_complete_event_rp0 *d = (hci_disconnection_complete_event_rp0 *) p_event_pckt->data;
    dbg_rec(3, d->Reason, d->Status, 0, (uint8_t *) &d->Connection_Handle, 2);
  }
  else if (p_event_pckt->evt == HCI_ENCRYPTION_CHANGE_EVT_CODE)
  {
    hci_encryption_change_event_rp0 *e = (hci_encryption_change_event_rp0 *) p_event_pckt->data;
    dbg_rec(5, e->Status, e->Encryption_Enabled, 0, 0, 0);
  }
  else if (p_event_pckt->evt == HCI_LE_META_EVT_CODE)
  {
    evt_le_meta_event *m = (evt_le_meta_event *) p_event_pckt->data;
    if (m->subevent == HCI_LE_ENHANCED_CONNECTION_COMPLETE_SUBEVT_CODE) dbg_rec(2, 0, 0, 0, m->data, 23);
    else if (m->subevent != HCI_LE_ADVERTISING_REPORT_SUBEVT_CODE) dbg_rec(7, m->subevent, 0, 0, m->data, 8);
  }
  else if (p_event_pckt->evt == HCI_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_DEBUG_EVT_CODE)
  {
    evt_blecore_aci *v = (evt_blecore_aci *) p_event_pckt->data;
    if ((v->ecode & 0xFF00) == 0x0C00) dbg_gatt_n++;
    else if (v->ecode != 0x0004) dbg_rec(6, v->ecode & 0xFF, v->ecode >> 8, 0, v->data, 8);
  }
  else
  {
    dbg_rec(8, p_event_pckt->evt, 0, 0, p_event_pckt->data, 8);
  }

  switch (p_event_pckt->evt)''')

SCR=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-hozakan-dev-FlySight-flysight-2-firmware--claude-worktrees-repo-status-ebc48f/5c1c2059-49eb-462a-9330-2c1db9a85699/scratchpad; cd $SCR/ipad; python3 - <<'EOF'

    ipad.py labels [bundle_id]            every labelled element: type, frame, label
    ipad.py tapl <bundle_id> <label>      tap the element whose label is EXACTLY <label>
                                          (refuses if none or several distinct frames match)
"""''')
s=s.replace('''def main():''','''def elements(bundle):
    import re
    reply = call({"action": "tree", "bundle_id": bundle}, timeout=60.0)
    if reply.get("result") != "tree":
        raise SystemExit(str(reply)[:300])
    out = []
    for line in reply["tree"].splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"\\s*(?:\\u2192)?(\\w+)(?: \\([^)]*\\))?, 0x[0-9a-f]+, \\{\\{([-\\d.]+), ([-\\d.]+)\\}, \\{([-\\d.]+), ([-\\d.]+)\\}\\}(.*)", line)
        if not m:
            continue
        rest = m.group(6)
        lab = re.search(r"label: '(.*?)'(?:,|$)", rest)
        val = re.search(r"value: (.*?)(?:,|$)", rest)
        out.append((m.group(1), float(m.group(2)), float(m.group(3)), float(m.group(4)), float(m.group(5)),
                    lab.group(1) if lab else None, val.group(1) if val else None, rest))
    return out


def main():''')
s=s.replace('''    elif cmd == "raw":''','''    elif cmd == "labels":
        for kind, x, y, w, h, lab, val, rest in elements(args[1] if len(args) > 1 else "com.apple.springboard"):
            if lab is not None or val is not None:
                flags = " [disabled]" if "Disabled" in rest else ""
                print(f"{kind:12s} ({x:6.1f},{y:6.1f} {w:6.1f}x{h:6.1f}) label={lab!r} value={val!r}{flags}")
    elif cmd == "tapl":
        hits = [(k, x, y, w, h) for k, x, y, w, h, lab, val, rest in elements(args[1]) if lab == args[2] and w > 0 and h > 0]
        buttons = [e for e in hits if e[0] in ("Button", "Cell", "Switch", "Link")]
        pick = buttons or hits
        frames = {e[1:] for e in pick}
        if len(frames) != 1:
            raise SystemExit(f"refusing to tap {args[2]!r}: {len(frames)} distinct matches {sorted(frames)}")
        k, x, y, w, h = pick[0]
        print(f"tap {k} {args[2]!r} at ({x + w / 2:.0f},{y + h / 2:.0f})", call({"action": "tap", "x": int(x + w / 2), "y": int(y + h / 2)}))
    elif cmd == "raw":''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

    private fun reconstructKnownDevices() {
        val storedInfos = deserializeDeviceList(lightStorageService.observe(KEY_KNOWN_DEVICES).value)
        val devices = storedInfos.mapNotNull { flySightApi.createDevice(it) }
        _knownDevices.value = devices
        val selectedId = lightStorageService.observe(KEY_SELECTED_DEVICE_ID).value
        _selectedDevice.value = devices.find { it.id == selectedId }
        // Known device: reconnect without scanning — on desktop createDevice/connect re-resolves
        // it via retrievePeripheralsWithIdentifiers. New devices go through the scan dialog.
        _selectedDevice.value?.let { device ->
            scope.launch {
                device.connect()
            }
        }
    }

        if (!ensureBluetoothReady()) {
            return

                        connectToDevice(device)
                    }
                }
            )
        )
    }

    override suspend fun ensureBluetoothReady(): Boolean {
        if (!permissionService.hasBluetoothPermission.value) {
            val granted = permissionService.requestPermission(Permission.Bluetooth)
            if (!granted) {
                return false
            }
        }
        return when (permissionService.bluetoothState.value) {
            BluetoothState.NotAvailable -> {
                false
            }
            BluetoothState.Disabled -> {
                permissionService.requestEnableBluetooth()
            }
            BluetoothState.Enabled -> {
                true
            }
        }
    }

    override fun addDevice(device: FlySightDevice) {

**Tool: Read** `/Users/hozakan/dev/FlySight/flysight-2-firmware/.claude/worktrees/repo-status-ebc48f/Docs/ble-pairing-fixes-report.html` (from line 128)
Result:

128	<p><strong>The starting hypothesis.</strong> Apple platforms never show an app the FlySight's address, only an opaque identifier. The suspicion was that, once the FlySight restarts pairing, the host can no longer map it to the device it bonded with.</p>
129	
130	<h2 id="found">What the investigation found</h2>
131	<ul>
132	  <li><strong>The hypothesis was not confirmed on macOS.</strong> Once bonded, the Mac shows the FlySight under one and the same identifier when it is idle, when it is back in pairing mode, and after the FlySight reboots. So the host does find the FlySight. What fails is the connection itself: the Mac's connection request is discarded by the FlySight's radio controller before the firmware hears of it (<a href="#b1">bug 1</a>).</li>
133	  <li><strong>Android is not affected</strong> because it connects in a different way, which the controller accepts. The difference between the platforms is in the address the <em>host</em> connects from, not in how it identifies the FlySight.</li>
134	  <li><strong>A FlySight that stops advertising</strong> was reproduced on <code>develop</code>: a pairing window that expires unused ends with no advertising at all (<a href="#b2">bug 2</a>). On <code>develop</code> the two chain: the bonded Mac cannot connect during the window, the window expires unused, and the FlySight goes silent.</li>
135	  <li><strong>iOS was not measured.</strong> Whether an iPhone or iPad fails for the same reason as the Mac, or for the identifier reason, is still open.</li>
136	  <li>A third, unrelated defect was found on the way (<a href="#b3">bug 3</a>).</li>
137	</ul>
138	
139	<table>
140	  <tr><th>#</th><th>Bug</th><th>Seen on</th><th>Proposed change</th></tr>
141	  <tr><td>1</td><td>A Mac that is already bonded can no longer connect, in pairing mode or idle</td><td><code>master</code>, <code>develop</code></td><td><code>app_ble.c</code>, <code>ble_count_bonded_devices()</code>: one call per bonded device</td></tr>
142	  <tr><td>2</td><td>A pairing window that expires unused leaves the FlySight advertising "pairing" for about 3.5 minutes, then not advertising at all</td><td><code>develop</code> (latent on <code>master</code>)</td><td><code>app_ble.c</code>, <code>Adv_Update()</code>: one statement</td></tr>
143	  <tr><td>3</td><td>The BLE keys are all zero on a first boot without <code>flysight.txt</code></td><td><code>master</code>, <code>develop</code></td><td><code>state.c</code>, <code>FS_State_Read()</code>: no early return before the keys are generated</td></tr>
144	</table>
145	<p>Each bug is described below as glossary, problem, proposed fix. Test results are in <a href="#tests">section 4</a>, the complete patch in <a href="#patch">section 5</a>.</p>

| Mac connects, FlySight idle | **fails** (timeout) | connects |

| Android connects, pairing mode and idle | connects | connects |

32:    *   **Adding Devices:** When a central device successfully completes the bonding process initiated during Pairing Request Mode, its address/identity is added to the FlySight's internal bonded device list, effectively whitelisting it for future connections.
34:    *   **Reconnecting with an identity address:** Bonded devices are also loaded into the controller's resolving list in *device privacy* mode, so a central may reconnect either from a resolvable private address or from its identity address. macOS connects from its public identity address; in the default *network privacy* mode the controller silently ignores such a request and the central just times out.
82:*   **Address:** Uses Random Private Resolvable Addresses (RPA). Central devices should support RPAs. Issues were observed when a central tried using Random Static Address after pairing.

114	<div class="meta">Prepared by Guillaume Imbert &middot; 7 October 2026 &middot; checked against <code>origin/master</code> (<code>9ec7186</code>) and <code>origin/develop</code> (<code>e67ee9f</code>). The same patch applies to both.</div>
115	
116	<h2 id="origin">The problem that started this</h2>
117	<ol>
118	  <li>Pair the FlySight with a macOS or iOS device that has never been paired with it.</li>
119	  <li>Disconnect.</li>
120	  <li>Start pairing again on the FlySight (double-press).</li>
121	</ol>
122	<table>
123	  <tr><th>Expected</th><td>The host finds the FlySight and is able to connect to it.</td></tr>
124	  <tr><th>Actual</th><td>The host cannot connect to the FlySight.</td></tr>
125	  <tr><th>Platforms</th><td>Seen on macOS and iOS. The same sequence works on Android.</td></tr>
126	</table>
127	<p><strong>Why step 3 happens in practice.</strong> Users start a new pairing to make the FlySight advertise again when it has stopped advertising. Bug 2 below is one way the FlySight ends up not advertising.</p>
128	<p><strong>The starting hypothesis.</strong> Apple platforms never show an app the FlySight's address, only an opaque identifier. The suspicion was that, once the FlySight restarts pairing, the host can no longer map it to the device it bonded with.</p>
129	
130	<h2 id="found">What the investigation found</h2>
131	<ul>
132	  <li><strong>The hypothesis was not confirmed on macOS.</strong> Once bonded, the Mac shows the FlySight under one and the same identifier when it is idle, when it is back in pairing mode, and after the FlySight reboots. So the host does find the FlySight. What fails is the connection itself: the Mac's connection request is discarded by the FlySight's radio controller before the firmware hears of it (<a href="#b1">bug 1</a>).</li>
133	  <li><strong>Android is not affected</strong> because it connects in a different way, which the controller accepts. The difference between the platforms is in the address the <em>host</em> connects from, not in how it identifies the FlySight.</li>
134	  <li><strong>A FlySight that stops advertising</strong> was reproduced on <code>develop</code>: a pairing window that expires unused ends with no advertising at all (<a href="#b2">bug 2</a>). On <code>develop</code> the two chain: the bonded Mac cannot connect during the window, the window expires unused, and the FlySight goes silent.</li>
135	  <li><strong>iOS was not measured.</strong> Whether an iPhone or iPad fails for the same reason as the Mac, or for the identifier reason, is still open.</li>
136	  <li>A third, unrelated defect was found on the way (<a href="#b3">bug 3</a>).</li>
137	</ul>

176	
177	<h3 class="step">Problem</h3>
178	<p><strong>What the user sees.</strong> The first pairing with a Mac works. After that, the Mac cannot connect to that FlySight again, whether the FlySight is idle or back in pairing mode. On the Mac the attempt simply never completes. The FlySight shows nothing either.</p>
179	<p><strong>To reproduce</strong> (<code>master</code> or <code>develop</code>, with a macOS app using CoreBluetooth):</p>
180	<ol>
181	  <li>Double-press to enter pairing mode, connect from the Mac, accept the pairing request.</li>
182	  <li>Disconnect.</li>
183	  <li>Try to connect again from the Mac, with the FlySight idle, or after a new double-press. The connection never happens.</li>
184	</ol>
185	<p><strong>What the firmware sees.</strong> An instrumented build recorded every HCI event delivered to <code>SVCCTL_App_Notification()</code>. During the Mac's attempts it recorded <em>nothing at all</em>: no connection event, no failure. With the fix below, the connection event appears, and shows how the two kinds of central differ:</p>
186	<pre><code><span class="cm"># Mac</span>
187	LE Enhanced Connection Complete   peer = FC:B2:14:**:**:** (public address)          peer RPA = none
188	<span class="cm"># Android phone (accepted with or without the fix)</span>
189	LE Enhanced Connection Complete   peer = 64:9D:38:**:**:** (identity, resolved)      peer RPA = 75:D8:EE:25:A8:07</code></pre>
190	<p>The Android phone connects from an RPA, which the controller resolves to the phone's identity. The Mac connects from its identity address, with no RPA.</p>
191	<p><strong>Cause.</strong> Each time advertising starts, <code>ble_count_bonded_devices()</code> rebuilds the controller's tables:</p>
192	<div class="file">STM32_WPAN/App/app_ble.c</div>
193	<pre><code>ret = aci_gap_configure_whitelist();                               <span class="cm">// accept list  = bonded devices</span>
194	ret = aci_gap_get_bonded_devices(&amp;total, devices);
195	...
196	ret = aci_gap_add_devices_to_resolving_list(total, rl_entries, 1); <span class="cm">// resolving list = bonded devices</span></code></pre>
197	<p>Entries are added in the default Network Privacy mode. From the moment the Mac is bonded, the controller therefore drops its connection requests, because they carry its identity address. Nothing is reported to the application, which is why the bug is invisible from the firmware side.</p>
198	<ul>
199	  <li>The first pairing works because the resolving list is still empty.</li>
200	  <li>Pairing mode does not help: it turns the accept list off, but the privacy rule belongs to the resolving list and still applies.</li>
201	  <li>Android is not affected, because it connects from an RPA. <strong>iOS was not tested</strong>; an iPhone normally uses RPAs too.</li>
202	</ul>
203
~~~~

## Assistant (22:03)

**Sur iPad, je n'ai pas confirmé le bug : avec les firmwares non modifiés, ton scénario fonctionne.** Le Mac reste le seul hôte qui échoue ; `master` câble débranché (Android compris) donne les mêmes résultats qu'avant.

## iPad (iPadOS 26.6.1, app SkyGames)

- **Appairé, il se reconnecte à chaque fois**, en 1 à 4 s : FlySight au repos, repassé en pairing mode, et après un redémarrage du FlySight. Vérifié sur `master` et `develop` strictement non modifiés, et sur les deux versions patchées.
- **Pourquoi il n'est pas touché par le bug 1** : il se connecte depuis une adresse privée résolvable, que le FlySight résout, comme Android. Le Mac, lui, se connecte depuis son adresse d'identité.
- **Ton hypothèse est vraie tant que l'iPad n'est pas appairé.** Avant l'appairage, l'app a listé la même carte sous 4 identifiants différents, un nouveau après chaque redémarrage de l'advertising. Un appareil choisi dans un scan fait avant le double appui reste sur « Connecting… » indéfiniment, et le FlySight n'enregistre aucune connexion.
- **L'ordre qui marche** : double appui d'abord, puis scan, puis choisir l'entrée qui vient d'apparaître. L'appairage est alors passé du premier coup.

Je me suis trompé tout à l'heure en attribuant mes deux premiers échecs à mon outillage : c'était cet identifiant périmé.

## Câble USB débranché, les quatre firmwares

| Firmware | Mac, repos | Mac, pairing mode | Android (les deux) | iPad (les deux) | Fenêtre de pairing non utilisée |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `master` non modifié | échec | échec | connecté | connecté | `01` 30 s puis `00`, advertise encore à 246 s |
| `master` + patch | connecté | connecté | connecté | connecté | `01` 30 s puis `00`, advertise encore à 244 s |
| `develop` non modifié | échec | échec | connecté | connecté | `01` pendant 194 s, puis plus d'advertising |
| `develop` + patch | connecté | connecté | connecté | connecté | `01` 30 s puis `00`, advertise encore à 248 s |

- **Carte** : remise sur le firmware de la branche avec les correctifs ; elle advertise normalement.
- **iPad** : j'ai activé le Bluetooth pour SkyGames. Il reste un appairage « FlySight » dans ses réglages Bluetooth et deux cartes FlySight dans SkyGames ; la première est l'identifiant périmé, à supprimer. La sonde est arrêtée.
- **Rien n'est commité.**

Si tu as vu l'échec sur un iPhone ou un iPad déjà appairé, il me faut les conditions exactes (version d'iOS, firmware du FlySight), parce que je ne le reproduis pas ici.

<ol>

</table>
<p><strong>Why step 3 happens in practice.</strong> Users start a new pairing to make the FlySight advertise again when it has stopped advertising. Bug 2 below is one way the FlySight ends up not advertising.</p>
<p><strong>The starting hypothesis.</strong> Apple platforms never show an app the FlySight's address, only an opaque identifier. The suspicion was that, once the FlySight restarts pairing, the host can no longer map it to the device it bonded with.</p>

Exit code 1
# FlySight 2 test CLI (ST-Link)

`vbus.py` drives a FlySight 2 through its ST-Link, so firmware can be tested
without touching the USB cable. There is no CLI over USB: the device only
enumerates as mass storage.

It makes the firmware believe the USB cable was unplugged or plugged back in,
while the cable stays connected. It takes over `VBUS_DIV` (PA2), the pin the
firmware uses to detect USB power (`FlySight/vbus.c`), so the real code path
runs: EXTI2 → mode state machine → `FS_USBMode_Init` / `FS_USBMode_DeInit`.

```bash
python vbus.py status                     # what the firmware and the host see
python vbus.py unplug                     # firmware sees VBUS low, host loses the device
python vbus.py plug                       # real VBUS again, host re-enumerates
python vbus.py cycle -n 20 --off 1 --on 1 # soak test, checks every transition
python vbus.py button                     # two clicks on the user button: BLE pairing mode
python vbus.py button press / release     # hold the button down, let go
python vbus.py reset                      # reset the MCU (clears any override)
python vbus.py reset-probe                # recover a stuck ST-Link
```

`unplug` and `plug` wait for the firmware (USB clock and D+ pull-up, read over SWD)
and for the host (`ioreg` on macOS, sysfs on Linux) to react, and print how long it
took. `cycle` also fails if the firmware faulted (CFSR/HFSR) and always gives the pin
back on exit, including on Ctrl-C. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 a check failed, 2 error.

`button` drives the user button (PC12, pressed when low) the same way. Only the sleep
mode reacts to it, so `unplug` first. The default two clicks start BLE pairing mode:
for 30 s the FlySight advertises with the pairing flag set and accepts any central.

## Requirements

- Python 3.7+, no packages to install.
- STM32CubeProgrammer or STM32CubeIDE (`STM32_Programmer_CLI` is found automatically,
  or pass `--programmer` / set `STM32_PROGRAMMER_CLI`) and an ST-Link on the SWD pins.
- **A firmware built with `CFG_DEBUGGER_SUPPORTED=1`** (CubeMX: STM32_WPAN → Debugger,
  or `Core/Inc/app_conf.h`). Otherwise `APPD_Init` switches PA13/PA14 to analog and
  disables debug in low-power modes, and the probe cannot reach the MCU while it runs
  (the tool reports this after `--swd-timeout`, default 10 s).

**Tool: Bash** — Commit the three firmware fixes separately, without any AI attribution

~~~~bash
set -e; git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Accept bonded centrals that connect from their identity address

ble_count_bonded_devices() loads every bonded device into the controller's
resolving list. Entries are added in the default Network Privacy mode, in
which the controller ignores a connection request that does not come from a
resolvable private address, and reports nothing to the application.

A Mac connects from its public identity address (measured on macOS 26). Once
bonded, it could therefore never connect again, whether the FlySight was idle
or back in pairing mode: pairing mode turns the accept list off, but the
privacy rule belongs to the resolving list and still applied. Android and
iPadOS connect from a resolvable private address and were not affected.

Switch each bonded entry to Device Privacy mode after the list is rebuilt, so
a bonded central may use either address.
EOF
git add STM32_WPAN/App/app_ble.c; git diff --cached | grep -E "^[+-]" | grep -v "^+++\|^---" | cut -c1-110; git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Clear the pairing request when the fast advertising period ends

When the 30 s pairing window ends without a connection, Adv_Update() restarts
advertising while request_pairing is still set, so the new advertising is
again in pairing configuration: limited discoverable, pairing flag set,
accept list off.

The mode update task only leaves pairing mode afterwards. It runs with the
tasks that use HCI commands, so it is paused while FS_Adv_Request() is in
progress, and APP_BLE_CancelPairing() then finds low power advertising
already running and does not restart it. The FlySight keeps advertising as
"pairing" for about 3.5 minutes, until the stack ends limited discoverable
mode, and then does not advertise at all until the next double press.

Clear the request in Adv_Update(), before advertising is restarted. This does
not depend on which task list the mode update task is in.
EOF
git add FlySight/state.c; git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Generate the BLE keys when flysight.txt cannot be opened

FS_State_Read() returned as soon as f_open() failed, before the device ID was
read and before the IRK and ERK were generated. On a first boot without
flysight.txt the BLE stack was therefore started with all-zero root keys,
and the next boot used different ones, read from the file written in the
meantime.

Move that last step to FS_State_Complete() and call it on both paths.
EOF
git log --format='%h %an <%ae>%n    %s' -3; git status --short

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	Simulate plugging / unplugging the USB cable of a FlySight 2 over SWD (ST-Link).
4	
5	The USB cable stays physically connected. The firmware decides that USB power
6	is present from one GPIO, PA2 (VBUS_DIV), an input with an interrupt on both
7	edges (see FlySight/vbus.c and FlySight/mode.c). This tool takes over that pin:
8	
9	  unplug  drives PA2 low (pin switched to output)
10	          -> firmware sees VBUS_LOW, leaves USB mode, stops the USB peripheral,
11	             the host sees the device disappear.
12	  plug    gives PA2 back (pin switched to input)
13	          -> the real VBUS level returns, the EXTI fires on the rising edge,
14	             firmware enters USB mode and the host enumerates it again.
15	
16	The firmware runs exactly the code path of a real unplug/plug (EXTI2 ->
17	FS_VBUS_Triggered -> mode state machine); it needs no test hook. The override
18	lives in the MCU's GPIO registers, so it survives this script exiting and is
19	cleared by any reset.
20	
21	Requires STM32_Programmer_CLI (STM32CubeProgrammer, also bundled with
22	STM32CubeIDE). SWD access is HOTPLUG: the core is never halted.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Record what the BLE stack reports to the firmware, and read it back over SWD.

The BLE controller can refuse a connection without telling the application
(see "Reconnecting with an identity address" in Docs/ble.md). To see that from
the FlySight side, this tool adds a temporary trace to app_ble.c:

  - a ring of the last 64 events in RAM: every advertising start (pairing mode
    or not, addresses in use), connection, disconnection, encryption change and
    GAP event;
  - two RAM switches that turn a fix off and on again without reflashing, so
    one boot and one bond can be compared with and without it:
      privacy  Device Privacy mode for bonded peers (ble_count_bonded_devices)
      window   request_pairing cleared in Adv_Update

The trace is test code. `instrument` edits the sources in place, `restore`
removes it again; it is never meant to be committed. It also sets
CFG_DEBUGGER_SUPPORTED to 1, which SWD access to a running firmware needs.

Usage:
    python ble_trace.py instrument          # then build and flash as usual
    python ble_trace.py read --elf build.elf
    python ble_trace.py mark --elf build.elf
    python ble_trace.py read --elf build.elf --since 12

"""
Tests for vbus.py that need no hardware.

Usage:
    python -m unittest test_vbus
"""

import types
import unittest

import vbus
from vbus import (GPIOA_BSRR, GPIOA_IDR, GPIOA_MODER, GPIOA_ODR, MODER_MASK,
                  MODER_OUTPUT, VBUS_BIT, State, Swd, SwdError)


class FakeGpioA:
    """Just enough of GPIOA for PA2: input follows VBUS, output follows ODR."""

    def __init__(self, vbus_present=True, moder=0x6ABFFBCF, odr=0x8000):
        self.vbus_present = vbus_present
        self.moder = moder
        self.odr = odr
        self.stuck_high = False
        self.writes = []

    def idr(self):
        out = (self.moder & MODER_MASK) == MODER_OUTPUT
        high = (self.odr & VBUS_BIT) != 0 if out else self.vbus_present
        if out and self.stuck_high:
            high = True
        return (0x8020 & ~VBUS_BIT) | (VBUS_BIT if high else 0)

    def read(self, *specs):
        values = []
        for addr, width in specs:
            word = {GPIOA_MODER: self.moder, GPIOA_IDR: self.idr(), GPIOA_ODR: self.odr}[addr]
            values.append(word & 0xFF if width == 8 else word)
        return values

    def write8(self, addr, value):

  (the tool reports this after `--swd-timeout`, default 10 s).

## Notes

- The override lives in the GPIO registers: it survives the script exiting and is
  cleared by any reset. Booting with VBUS low cannot be simulated this way, because
  the firmware reconfigures PA2 during start-up.
- Use `--vid` / `--pid` if the USB descriptor changes, `--no-host` when the cable is
  not plugged into the machine running the script, `--sn` with several ST-Links.
- The ST-Link can get stuck when an SWD access is interrupted (libusb timeouts,
  `ST-LINK SN : -`). `reset-probe` resets it at USB level; unplugging it also works.

~~~~bash
set -e; SCR=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-hozakan-dev-FlySight-flysight-2-firmware--claude-worktrees-repo-status-ebc48f/5c1c2059-49eb-462a-9330-2c1db9a85699/scratchpad; git add Scripts/cli/ble_trace.py Scripts/cli/test_ble_trace.py Scripts/cli/README.md; git diff --cached --stat; git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Add ble_trace.py, a temporary BLE trace read over SWD

The BLE controller can refuse a connection without reporting anything to the
application, which is how a bonded Mac failed to reconnect with nothing to
see in a normal build.

`ble_trace.py instrument` adds a trace to app_ble.c: the last 64 advertising
starts, connections (with the address and address type of the central),
disconnections, encryption changes and GAP events, kept in RAM. `read` prints
them over SWD while the firmware runs. `set privacy|window on|off` flips a
RAM switch that turns one of the two advertising fixes off and on again, so
the same boot and the same bond can be compared with and without it.

The trace is test code and is not part of the firmware: `restore` gives back
the exact original sources, and the tests fail if an instrumented tree is
committed or if a change in app_ble.c breaks one of the hooks.
EOF

metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When committing on the FlySight firmware repo, keep each concern in its own commit: firmware fixes (one per bug), the test CLI (`Scripts/cli`), the dev-environment tooling (the USB plug/unplug switch), and the tooling used to test a bug (SWD switches, traces).

**Why:** the user said on 2026-10-08 "fait bien attention à avoir un commit pour la cli, un commit pour l'environnement de dev (aka le switch usb actif/inactif) et un commit pour les tests sur le bug (le switch SWD etc)". The fixes are meant to be merged by the FlySight creator, so they must be takeable without the tooling. My reading of the three labels was partly a guess (the user's wording was short).

**How to apply:** split hunks of one file across commits when they belong to different bugs (`git apply --cached` with a filtered patch). Test tooling that only exists in a scratch directory is worth bringing into the repo as its own commit when the user asks for "a commit for the tests". No AI attribution, see [[no-ai-signature-in-commits]].

## Assistant (22:31)

C'est commité, en cinq commits séparés sur `claude/repo-status-ebc48f`, sans aucune signature d'IA et sans push.

| Commit | Contenu |
|---|---|
| `8720e69` Accept bonded centrals that connect from their identity address | correctif du bug 1 (`app_ble.c`, une ligne dans `Docs/ble.md`) |
| `bddd707` Clear the pairing request when the fast advertising period ends | correctif du bug 2 (`app_ble.c`) |
| `47e458f` Generate the BLE keys when flysight.txt cannot be opened | correctif du bug 3 (`state.c`) |
| `0d25f3e` vbus.py: add a button command | la CLI : appui sur le bouton via SWD (double clic = pairing mode) |
| `e7d8d66` Add ble_trace.py, a temporary BLE trace read over SWD | les tests sur le bug : trace BLE et interrupteurs des correctifs pilotés par SWD |

- **Bascule USB actif/inactif** : je n'ai pas créé de nouveau commit, elle était déjà dans l'historique (`77c065e` et `cea07c5`, `vbus.py plug/unplug`). Ce commit `77c065e` contient à la fois la CLI et la bascule USB ; si tu veux les séparer, il faut réécrire ce commit, dis-le-moi.
- **Outillage de test** : il n'existait que dans un dossier temporaire. Je l'ai remis au propre dans `Scripts/cli/ble_trace.py` avec ses tests, et j'ai rejoué dessus le test Mac sur la carte (correctif coupé : échec et aucune connexion enregistrée ; correctif actif : connecté). Les 45 tests de `Scripts/cli` passent.
- **Rapport** : [Docs/ble-pairing-fixes-report.html](Docs/ble-pairing-fixes-report.html) n'est pas commité, tu ne l'avais pas listé. Dis-moi si tu le veux dans un commit à part.
- **Découpage** : j'ai interprété « le switch SWD » comme l'interrupteur qui coupe un correctif via SWD. Si tu pensais au bouton piloté par SWD, c'est le commit `0d25f3e`.

Tes deux questions sur le rapport :

- **Ta séquence** : la phrase que tu cites vient d'une ancienne version, elle n'est plus dans le fichier (recharge la page). J'ai quand même repris la section d'ouverture avec tes mots : les trois étapes, attendu, constaté, « The issue does not appear on Android », et ton hypothèse sur l'adresse MAC masquée par iOS.
- **« latent on master »** : ça voulait dire que le code fautif est présent sur `master` mais que le symptôme ne s'y produit pas. Le mot était obscur, je l'ai remplacé par cette phrase, avec un renvoi à l'explication du bug 2.

Le rapport liste aussi maintenant les trois commits de correctifs, pour qu'ils puissent être repris un par un. La carte est revenue sur le firmware de la branche.

134	  <li><strong>A FlySight that stops advertising</strong> was reproduced on <code>develop</code>: a pairing window that expires unused ends with no advertising at all (<a href="#b2">bug 2</a>). 135	  <li><strong>On the iPad tested, the sequence works, on unmodified firmware.</strong> Once bonded, an iPad (iPadOS 26.6.1) reconnects with the FlySight idle, back in pairing mode, and after a FlySight reboot, on unmodified <code>master</code> and <code>develop</code>. Like Android, it connects in the way the controller accepts, so bug 1 does not reach it.</li>
136	  <li><strong>The hypothesis does hold for an Apple host that is not bonded.</strong> The FlySight advertises from a private address that changes each time advertising restarts. A host without the bond cannot follow it: before pairing, the iPad listed the same FlySight under four different identifiers over four advertising runs. An app that picked the FlySight from a scan made before pairing mode started then waits forever on an identifier that no longer exists. This is how BLE privacy is meant to behave, not a firmware defect, and no firmware change is proposed for it. Scanning after pairing mode has started avoids it.</li>
137	  <li>A third, unrelated defect was found on the way (<a href="#b3">bug 3</a>).</li>

207	<h3 class="step">Proposed fix</h3>
208	<p>Put each bonded peer's entry in Device Privacy mode, right after the resolving list is filled. The list is rebuilt at every advertising start, so the setting is re-applied each time.</p>
209	<div class="file">STM32_WPAN/App/app_ble.c &mdash; ble_count_bonded_devices()</div>

215	   }
216	<span class="add">+
217	+  // 4) Let bonded peers connect with their identity address too. Entries of the
218	+  //    resolving list default to Network Privacy mode, where the controller
219	+  //    silently ignores a connection request that does not use a resolvable
220	+  //    private address. A Mac connects from its public identity address
221	+  //    (measured on macOS 26), so without this a bonded Mac never reaches us,
222	+  //    in pairing mode or not.

233	<p><code>BLE_PRIVACY_MODE_DEVICE</code> is a new local constant, <code>0x01</code>, the value defined by the specification.</p>
234	<p><strong>What changes, and what does not.</strong> The FlySight keeps advertising with RPAs, and the accept list keeps working as before. The one thing that widens: a connection request carrying a bonded peer's identity address is now accepted at link level. Whoever sends it still cannot read or write anything, because the FlySight's characteristics require an encrypted link and encryption needs the bond keys; a link that stays idle is closed by the existing 30-second inactivity timeout.</p>
235

237	<h2 id="b2"><span class="num">2.</span>Bug 2: an unused pairing window ends in silence</h2>
238	
239	<h3 class="step">Glossary</h3>
240	<dl>
241	  <dt>Pairing window</dt>
242	  <dd>The 30 seconds after a double-press, during which <code>request_pairing</code> is set: the FlySight advertises the pairing flag (<code>01</code>) and the accept list is off.</dd>
243	  <dt>Fast and low-power advertising</dt>
244	  <dd><code>FS_Adv_Request(APP_BLE_FAST_ADV)</code> advertises every 80&ndash;100 ms and starts a 30-second timer. When the timer fires, <code>Adv_Update()</code> calls <code>FS_Adv_Request(APP_BLE_LP_ADV)</code>, which restarts advertising at the slow rate with no timer.</dd>
245	  <dt>Limited discoverable mode</dt>
246	  <dd>The stack mode used for pairing advertising (<code>aci_gap_set_limited_discoverable()</code>). The stack ends it by itself after about three minutes and raises <code>ACI_GAP_LIMITED_DISCOVERABLE_VSEVT_CODE</code>. Normal advertising (<code>aci_gap_set_undirected_connectable()</code>) has no such limit.</dd>
247	  <dt>Sequencer tasks "with" and "without" HCI command</dt>
248	  <dd>The two task lists in <code>app_conf.h</code>. While one HCI command waits for its answer, <code>BLE_StatusNot()</code> pauses every task of the first list; tasks of the second list keep running.</dd>
249	</dl>
250	
251	<h3 class="step">Problem</h3>
252	<p><strong>What the user sees.</strong> Double-press, then nobody connects. After 30 seconds the LED goes off as expected. But a scanner still sees the FlySight advertising "pairing mode" for another three minutes, and after that the FlySight cannot be found or reached at all, by any device, until the button is pressed again. Unplugging and replugging USB does not bring it back.</p>

EOF

Le rapport parle maintenant de macOS, et il a une nouvelle section 4, « Behaviour changes, commit by commit » : [Docs/ble-pairing-fixes-report.html](Docs/ble-pairing-fixes-report.html).

## Sur iOS, pour être exact

Je ne t'avais pas dit qu'un commit changeait le comportement sur iOS, ou alors je me suis mal exprimé. Voici ce qui est mesuré :

| Commit | macOS | iOS (iPad) | Android |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Adresse d'identité acceptée | un Mac appairé peut se reconnecter (avant : jamais) | aucun changement | aucun changement |
| 2. Fin de la fenêtre de pairing | sur `develop`, identique partout : après une fenêtre non utilisée le FlySight reste joignable (avant : injoignable après environ 3,5 min) | idem | idem |
| 3. Clés BLE sans `flysight.txt` | identique partout : vraies clés dès le premier démarrage, stables ensuite | idem | idem |

Le commit 2 change donc bien quelque chose sur iOS, comme sur toutes les plateformes. Je viens de le mesurer avec l'iPad appairé sur `develop`, en appuyant sur Connect 246 s après un double appui que personne n'a utilisé :

- **Sans le patch** : pas de connexion en 25 s. Un nouveau double appui, et l'iPad se connecte 2,5 s après.
- **Avec le patch** : connecté en 1,3 s.

## Ce qui a changé dans le rapport

- **Ouverture** : ta séquence est écrite pour un Mac (« Pair to an unpaired Mac », attendu, constaté, hypothèse sur l'adresse MAC masquée par macOS). iOS et Android apparaissent comme non touchés.
- **Identifiant** : le changement d'identifiant vu sur l'iPad non appairé est devenu une remarque à part, sans changement firmware proposé.
- **Section 4** : pour chaque commit, un tableau situation / avant / après, avec pour chaque ligne si c'est mesuré, déduit du code ou non testé.

Deux changements de comportement que le créateur du FlySight doit connaître, tous deux dans la section :

- **Commit 1** : une demande de connexion portant l'adresse d'identité d'un hôte appairé est maintenant acceptée au niveau lien, même si elle vient d'un autre appareil. Il ne peut rien lire ni écrire sans les clés, et le lien inactif est coupé au bout de 30 s. C'est le fonctionnement prévu de ce mode, je ne l'ai pas testé.
- **Commit 2** : sur `develop` sans le patch, on pouvait encore appairer jusqu'à environ 3,5 min après le double appui. Avec le patch c'est 30 s, comme sur `master` et comme le dit `Docs/ble.md`. La durée est mesurée ; que la liste d'acceptation reste ouverte pendant ce temps vient de la lecture du code.

Le rapport n'est toujours pas commité. La carte est revenue sur le firmware de la branche, l'iPad est déconnecté et la sonde arrêtée.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn the session transcript (JSONL) into one readable Markdown file."""
import json
import re
import sys

SRC, DST = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
MAX_LINES, MAX_CHARS = 80, 4000

REDACTIONS = [
    (re.compile(r"\d{6,}-[a-z0-9]{20,}\.apps\.googleusercontent\.com"), "[google-client-id]"),
    (re.compile(r"Livebox-[0-9A-F]{4}"), "[wifi-ssid]"),
    (re.compile(r"[calendar event]"), "[calendar event]"),
]


def clean(text):
    for rx, repl in REDACTIONS:
        text = rx.sub(repl, text)
    return text.replace("~~~ ~", "~~~ ~")


def clip(text, max_lines=MAX_LINES, max_chars=MAX_CHARS):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    note = ""
    if len(lines) > max_lines:
        head, tail = max_lines - 15, 15
        note = f"[... {len(lines) - head - tail} lines omitted ...]"
        lines = lines[:head] + [note] + lines[-tail:]
    out = "\n".join(lines)
    if len(out) > max_chars:
        out = out[:max_chars] + f"\n[... output cut at {max_chars} characters, {len(text)} in total ...]"
    return out


def fence(text, lang=""):
    return f"~~~ ~{lang}\n{clean(text).rstrip()}\n~~~ ~\n"


def result_text(content):
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content
    parts = []
    for c in content or []:
[... 116 lines omitted ...]
  place and the size of each cut are marked. Screenshots are left out.
- The assistant's private reasoning and the application's own system messages are not included.
- Three things are replaced by a placeholder: a Google OAuth client ID, a Wi-Fi network
  name and a calendar entry that appeared in tool output.
- Paths under `/private/tmp/claude-501/.../scratchpad` were temporary files on the Mac.
  The parts worth keeping were committed to the firmware repository as `Scripts/cli/`.

The conclusions are in `ble-pairing-fixes-report.html`, next to this file. Earlier statements
in the conversation were sometimes wrong and corrected later; the report is the reference.
"""
with open(DST, "w") as f:
    f.write(header + "".join(out))
print(counts, sum(len(x) for x in out) + len(header))
EOF

**Tool: Bash** — Put the report and the full export in debug_ble, add a short index, and regenerate the readable conversation

~~~~bash
set -e; SCR=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-hozakan-dev-FlySight-flysight-2-firmware--claude-worktrees-repo-status-ebc48f/5c1c2059-49eb-462a-9330-2c1db9a85699/scratchpad; mv Docs/ble-pairing-fixes-report.html debug_ble/ble-pairing-fixes-report.html; mv /Users/hozakan/Downloads/session-export-1791415689385.zip debug_ble/conversation-raw.zip; unzip -l debug_ble/conversation-raw.zip | tail -8; printf 'conversation-raw.zip\n' > debug_ble/.gitignore; cat > debug_ble/README.md <<'EOF'
# debug_ble

Material from the FlySight 2 BLE investigation done on macOS, Android and iPadOS, put
together to continue the work on Windows and Linux.

| File | What it is |
|------|------------|
| `ble-pairing-fixes-report.html` | The conclusions: the three firmware bugs, their fixes, what each commit changes in behaviour, and the test results. Open it in a browser. Start here. |
| `conversation.md` | The whole session in readable form: every message, every command that was run and its output (long outputs are shortened, screenshots left out). |
| `conversation-raw.zip` | The same session as exported by the Claude desktop app, complete and unshortened. It contains screenshots of personal devices, so it is ignored by git here; copy it by hand if it is needed. |

## Where the code is

- **Firmware**: this repository, branch `claude/repo-status-ebc48f`. One commit per fix
  (`app_ble.c` twice, `state.c`), plus the test tools in `Scripts/cli`: `vbus.py` (USB
  plug/unplug and button over the ST-Link) and `ble_trace.py` (what the BLE stack reports
  to the firmware, read over SWD). Both are plain Python and only need
  `STM32_Programmer_CLI`; see `Scripts/cli/README.md`.
- **App**: the SkyGames repository, submodule `Libs/FlySightApi`. The native BLE layer is in
  `core/src/nativeInterop/c/` with one folder per platform (`macos`, `linux`, `windows`).
  At the time of this export its changes were not committed, and the Linux and Windows
  files had been edited but never compiled.

## Nothing has been measured on Windows or Linux yet

What decided the outcome on each platform so far is the address the host connects from
once it is bonded: the Mac uses its identity address and hits bug 1, Android and iPadOS use
a resolvable private address and do not. `ble_trace.py read` shows which one a host uses
(`CONNECTED ... peer=... (public)` against `(public identity (resolved))`), and whether its
connection request reaches the firmware at all.
EOF

# FlySight 2 BLE investigation: full conversation

Export of the Claude Code session in which the FlySight 2 BLE problems were investigated
on macOS, Android and iPadOS. It starts with an earlier task of the same session (a CLI that
fakes USB plug/unplug over the ST-Link), which built the bench used later.

- 50 user messages, 190 assistant messages, 964 tool calls, in chronological order.
- The user writes mostly in French; the assistant answers in French or English.
- Every tool call is shown with its command. Long commands and outputs are shortened; the
  place and the size of each cut are marked. Screenshots are left out.
- The assistant's private reasoning and the application's own system messages are not included.
- Three things are replaced by a placeholder: a Google OAuth client ID, a Wi-Fi network

    private val delegate: BluetoothServiceDelegate
) : BluetoothService {

    /**
     * flysightble-style escalation around the lifecycle-bound delegate scan:
     * scan for [SCAN_PHASES_MS]\[0] ms; if still no device, extend by the next phase;
     * stop as soon as at least one device was seen at a checkpoint, or once all phases
     * are exhausted.
     */
    override fun scan(): Flow<List<BluetoothDeviceInfo>> = channelFlow {
        var latest: List<BluetoothDeviceInfo> = emptyList()
        val job = launch {
            delegate.scan().collect { snapshot ->
                latest = snapshot
                send(snapshot)
            }
        }
        for (phase in SCAN_PHASES_MS) {
            delay(phase)
            if (latest.isNotEmpty()) {
                break
            }
        }
        job.cancel()
        close()
    }

    private val scanStream: () -> Flow<ScanResult>,
    private val knownDeviceIds: () -> Set<String>,

) : DialogItem {

    @Composable

        var retryKey by remember { mutableStateOf(0) }
        var devices by remember { mutableStateOf<List<FlySightDevice>>(emptyList()) }
        var scanning by remember { mutableStateOf(true) }
        var errorMessage by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }

        LaunchedEffect(retryKey) {
            devices = emptyList()
            errorMessage = null
            scanning = true
            scanStream().collect { result ->
                when (result) {
                    is ScanResult.Success -> {
                        val knownIds = knownDeviceIds()
                        devices = result.devices.filter { it.id !in knownIds }

p='debug_ble/ble-pairing-fixes-report.html'; s=open(p).read()
a=s.index('<p><strong>A side observation, with no firmware change proposed.</strong>')
b=s.index('</p>', a)+4
new='''<p><strong>An app-side issue, not a firmware one.</strong> For a host that is <em>not</em> bonded, the identifier does change. The FlySight advertises from a private address that changes each time advertising restarts, and only a bonded host can follow it. Before it was paired, the iPad listed the same FlySight under four different identifiers over four advertising runs. An entry obtained before pairing mode started is therefore dead once pairing mode starts: an app that still offers it, or that has saved it, waits forever on an identifier that no longer exists. This is how BLE privacy is meant to behave, so the handling belongs in the app: its scan list must only hold what is advertising now, and it should not keep a FlySight it has never connected to.</p>'''
s=s[:a]+new+s[b:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

## Assistant (23:49)

D'accord. J'ai remis le titre et le texte du bug 1 comme ils étaient : « a bonded Mac can no longer connect », au repos comme en pairing mode.

Puisque tu me suis, voici exactement sur quoi ça repose :

- **Mesuré** : sur `master` et `develop` non modifiés, le Mac déjà appairé échoue au repos juste après un démarrage, sans aucun passage en pairing mode. Et sur un même démarrage, en coupant puis en réactivant le correctif : actif il se connecte, coupé il échoue, réactivé il se connecte.
- **Pas fait** : un appairage tout neuf sur firmware non modifié, suivi aussitôt d'une tentative au repos. Les échecs au repos ont tous été mesurés avec un appairage qui existait déjà. Je l'ai ajouté aux limites du rapport. Pour le faire il faut rebrancher l'USB, afin d'effacer les appairages du FlySight.

Sur ton message précédent (la liste à vider au démarrage d'un scan) :

- **Le rapport** dit maintenant que c'est un problème côté app, pas firmware.
- **Mais l'app vide déjà sa liste au démarrage d'un scan**, à deux endroits : la boîte de dialogue de scan (`FlySightScanDialogComposables.kt`) et le scanner Apple de la bibliothèque. Ce n'est donc pas ça qui manque.
- **Les deux vrais trous**, vus sur l'iPad et dans le code :
  - Pendant un scan, une entrée qui n'émet plus n'est jamais retirée, et la liste reste figée à l'écran une fois le scan terminé (10 s).
  - Un FlySight choisi est enregistré tout de suite, avant d'avoir réussi à se connecter (`DefaultFlySightService.addNewDevice()`). C'est ce qui laisse une carte bloquée sur « Connecting… ».

Je n'ai pas modifié SkyGames : j'ai créé une tâche séparée qui décrit ces deux points, à lancer quand tu veux.

Le rapport et `conversation.md` dans [debug_ble/](debug_ble/) sont à jour ; le zip brut date de l'export précédent.

+    *   Device State terminal/mode commands may also be written blind. If indications are disabled and the command is accepted, FlySight schedules the requested action without sending a response.

I couldn't find Microsoft documentation that says which own-address type Windows 11 uses when it initiates an LE connection, so these results don't answer that directly. Here's what they do cover.

**BLE address basics**
- As mentioned above, all Bluetooth LE devices must use either a public address or a random static address, where the latter is far more common. (Nordic's course material places a device's identity address in one of those two categories.)
- Argenox notes that most BLE products avoid public addresses, partly because public addresses can be tracked.
- Random private addresses rotate over time, which makes it harder to follow a device. This is an address that changes periodically and is used to hide the device's identity and to deter device tracking.
- Peers that hold the Identity Resolving Key can work out each new rotating address. The pre-shared key is the Identity Resolving Key (IRK) and is used both to generate and to resolve the random address.
- The rotating value stands in for the real identity, which remains either the public or the random static address.

**Initiator-side privacy in another stack**
Silicon Labs' host stack includes events that report when its scanner/initiator moves to a new private address (New events sl_bt_evt_gap_random_address_refresh and sl_bt_evt_advertiser_random_address_refresh notify the application when the scanner/initiator or a stack-managed advertiser starts using a new private address.). This shows that initiator-side address rotation is a normal feature of BLE stacks, but it says nothing about Windows.

**Windows-specific results**
- Microsoft's PublicTargetAddress reference describes a section data type for a list of public Bluetooth LE target addresses. That is an advertising payload field, so in my reading it doesn't control the address a Windows host uses when it connects.
- Zebra's Windows 11 setup walkthrough has you open the Advanced tab of the Bluetooth LE Generic Attribute Service properties and note the address. It doesn't say whether that address is public or random.
